Tyrande now governs the kaldorei from Darnassus as the night elves take their place in the Alliance. When the Burning Legion returned during the Third War, she woke the sleeping druids to face the danger. Though she mistrusted the newly arrived orcs and humans, she helped forge a desperate coalition at Mount Hyjal. The night elves gave up their immortality at Nordrassil to destroy Archimonde.

Mount Hyjal still bears the scars of that battle, and Malfurion is again occupied with guarding the Emerald Dream. From the grand Temple of the Moon, Tyrande watches for Horde incursions.

npc:verner-osgood.text: Verner Osgood. Outside Lakeshire’s smithy, Verner Osgood keeps the forge at work. He must meet the Stormwind Guard’s need for horseshoes, weapons, and armor while gnolls raid the hills. Verner Osgood keeps Lakeshire’s forge working, making horseshoes and other supplies for the town. The Stormwind Guard continually requisitions his stock for weapons and armor. With the kingdom’s forces stretched thin and local garrisons short on supplies, Verner bears much of the burden of equipping Redridge’s defenders. Gnoll raids threaten Verner’s work and the town’s horses. Packs ambush livestock in the Redridge hills and seize working horses that stray beyond Lakeshire. Verner recruits travelers to hunt the marauders and their packleader, Yowler.

npc:viktori-prism-antras.text: Viktori Prism'Antras. Above Darkshire, Viktori Prism'Antras keeps watch on the stars. In Duskwood's gloom, he hopes a telescope will bring them into clear view. Beyond the gryphon roost, up the slope, Viktori Prism'Antras peers into Duskwood's gloom. Undead incursions, ravenous spiders, and creeping shadows surround him. Yet he looks past the suffocating canopy, hoping to build a fine telescope that brings the stars into clear focus. In the heavens, he seeks quiet refuge from the dread engulfing the hamlet. Building a delicate telescope takes work in this cursed forest. Viktori follows blueprints from his gnomish friend, Cog Glitzspinner. He asks passersby to find rare materials for crafting lenses and mechanical housings. Finely cut glass and metal lenses lie scattered across perilous ground.

npc:warden-thelwater.text: Warden Thelwater. At the Stockade entrance in Stormwind, Warden Thelwater faces a prison riot. He calls for capable adventurers to stop the Defias prisoners before the uprising reaches the city above. Beneath Stormwind's canals, the Stockade holds the kingdom's most dangerous miscreants, petty thieves, and political conspirators. Warden Thelwater was charged with keeping them locked away. Then an organized revolt caught the guards off guard. The prisoners overwhelmed security and seized the cells, leaving Thelwater barricaded at the entrance as he struggles to contain an armed uprising beneath the capital's streets.

npc:william-pestle.text: William Pestle. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, William Pestle gathers supplies for Stormwind's apothecary. He and his brother Morgan run the shop in the Trade District. William hires travelers to find candles, kelp, and herbs. William works from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. His brother Morgan Pestle tends the counter at Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind City's Trade District. In Elwynn Forest, William works with local gatherers to secure raw materials for the city's shops. He sends regular shipments to Stormwind, where citizens rely on restorative salves, draughts, and powders. Common garden herbs do not always meet William's needs. He hires newcomers to gather wax candles carried by Elwynn's kobolds and crystal kelp from the murlocs of Crystal Lake, just east of Goldshire. The ingredients may seem strange to those unfamiliar with alchemy. William believes they have potent virtues in a mixture.

npc:wizbang-cranktoggle.text: Wizbang Cranktoggle. In Auberdine, Wizbang Cranktoggle keeps Darkshore’s buzzboxes working. The eccentric gnome engineer lives upstairs at the inn, far from the halls of Gnomeregan and Ironforge. Wizbang Cranktoggle brings Alliance ingenuity to Auberdine. The gnome engineer works on the inn’s upper floor, among tools and spare parts. The night elves here seek harmony with nature and follow ancient customs. Wizbang tackles practical mechanical problems instead, far from Kalimdor’s solemn druidic traditions. Along Darkshore’s rugged coast, Wizbang maintains a network of buzzboxes. The devices send automated reports and carry messages over long distances. Coastal weather and hostile wildlife often damage them. So Wizbang asks travelers to find parts, salvage tools such as gaffer jacks, and recover electropellers to keep the network working.

subzone:addle-s-stead.text: Addle's Stead. In southwestern Duskwood, Addle's Stead lies abandoned south of Raven Hill. Its first homesteaders fled long ago. Now the Defias Brotherhood uses the farm as a hidden staging ground. Addle's Stead lies in ruin beneath Duskwood's darkness. The Defias Brotherhood now uses the old farm. Agents watch the perimeter and lurk in the farmhouse, while supplies fill the barn. Shadows in southwestern Duskwood help them evade the Night Watch and Stormwind authorities.

subzone:aldrassil.text: Aldrassil. Young kaldorei gather beneath Aldrassil’s vast boughs in Shadowglen. Its hollowed trunk shelters trainers, merchants, and local leaders. Aldrassil shelters young night elves in Shadowglen. Ramps wind through its immense trunk, past trainers and artisans, and climb to the high roost. Tenaron Stormgrip watches over the glade’s protection from there. Beyond the tree, Teldrassil stretches across the horizon. Beneath Aldrassil’s canopy, novices learn their arts before venturing into Kalimdor’s troubled wilds.

subzone:alexston-farmstead.text: Alexston Farmstead. Wild Harvest Watchers prowl the ruined fields at Alexston Farmstead. Baros Alexston grew up here before becoming Stormwind's city architect. You find Alexston Farmstead among Westfall's dry plains, abandoned like the neighboring estates. Its caretakers fled as banditry spread across the countryside. The fields have gone wild, and Harvest Watchers left to tend the crops now attack anyone near the barren farmhouse. Baros Alexston worked these fields in his youth, then left to pursue masonry and construction. He became one of Stormwind's most prominent citizens and helped design parts of the rebuilt capital. Something from his early life remains among the ruins.

subzone:algaz-station.text: Algaz Station. At Algaz Station, Mountaineers keep watch over the northern road from Loch Modan to the Wetlands. South of Dun Algaz, the outpost guards the mountain pass. Dwarven Mountaineers watch the road north from Loch Modan at Algaz Station. East of North Gate Pass and south of Dun Algaz, the post guards the route between Ironforge and the northern lowlands. Trade and troops travel through the mountain tunnels, though beasts and troggs threaten the hills. The Mountaineers keep the way open and give weary travelers a place to rest, make repairs, and find martial support before entering the pass.

subzone:alterac-mountains.text: Alterac Mountains. In the Alterac Mountains, ruined settlements and bandits claim the slopes above Hillsbrad’s pastures. Once the heart of a proud human kingdom, the highlands now offer travelers little safety. The Alterac highlands once held a sovereign human nation, one of seven kingdoms born from ancient Arathor. During the Second War, King Aiden Perenolde secretly made a pact with the Old Horde. He let orcish forces cross the peaks in return for his kingdom’s safety. The Alliance of Lordaeron uncovered the betrayal and deposed him. Martial law and territorial disputes left the region divided. The Third War’s devastation left the mountains lawless. Disinherited nobles formed the Syndicate, which works from Strahnbrad’s ruins and plots to reclaim its lost dominion through sabotage and assassination. Crushridge ogres hold the shattered capital. Gnolls roam the slopes, and the magical ruins around Dalaran lie shattered. Alterac’s passes remain among Lordaeron’s most perilous paths.

subzone:alther-s-mill.text: Alther's Mill. Northeast of Lakeshire, Alther's Mill lies in ruins, its old grounds haunted by scavengers and predators. Travelers bound east for Stonewatch pass this grim mark of the frontier. Alther's Mill once supplied timber to Lakeshire and nearby settlements. Its clearing northeast of Lake Everstill gave the millers access to timber in the mountains. As trouble spread through Stormwind's kingdom, the Blackrock clan descended from the heights of Stonewatch. The millers abandoned their work, leaving the timber buildings and wheel to decay. Monstrous tarantulas, carrion vultures, and raiders took the mill after its workers left. Travelers on the path to the eastern passes must skirt the shadowed grounds with care. Shadowy operatives and thieves also use the abandoned compound. Its discarded storage boxes and hidden corners give them room to practice lockpicking and carry out covert trades beyond the Lakeshire Town Watch's gaze.

subzone:amberstill-ranch.text: Amberstill Ranch. North of Gol'Bolar Quarry, Amberstill Ranch stands along the snowy road to Loch Modan. The Amberstill family tends its mountain rams and guards them from hungry predators. Across Khaz Modan, Amberstill Ranch is known for its strong mountain rams. The Amberstill family tends the stables and paddocks, training the sure-footed beasts for snowy passes and steep cliffs. The ranch supplies riding mounts and livestock. Wendigos drawn to the flock threaten the herd, and the family must fend them off.

subzone:ameth-aran.text: Ameth'Aran. Broken colonnades rise from Ameth'Aran in southern Darkshore, where restless ghosts haunt the stones. Once a great Highborne city, it fell when the Well of Eternity collapsed and shattered the ancient world. Before the Great Sundering, Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran were twin centers of Highborne influence along the ancient coastline. Queen Azshara favored Ameth'Aran, where its ruling nobles pursued unrestrained arcane experiments. Their sorcerer, Athrikus Narassin, governed from afar in the Tower of Althalaxx. The city flourished until the Well of Eternity collapsed and tore the Kaldorei Empire apart.

subzone:angerfang-encampment.text: Angerfang Encampment. At Angerfang Encampment, Dragonmaw orcs gather in the central Wetlands and threaten nearby dwarven settlements. Chieftain Nek'rosh Skullcrusher leads the renegades as they prepare to strike Menethil Harbor. Dragonmaw warriors hold the marsh around Angerfang Encampment in the central Wetlands. Barricades and watchtowers guard their camp, where warriors, bonewarders, and dark spellcasters loyal to the old ways gather. From there, the clan raids travelers on the roads and menaces nearby dwarven digs, including Whelgar's Excavation Site.

subzone:anvilmar.text: Anvilmar. In Coldridge Valley, Anvilmar gathers young Bronzebeard dwarves and displaced gnomes to train for the road ahead. Snowy Dun Morogh surrounds the fortified outpost and its great stone forge. A great forge burns inside Anvilmar's sturdy stone walls in the northern crags of Coldridge Valley. Class mentors and supply vendors serve the outpost, while veteran mountain mountaineers drill recruits before they set out across the kingdom. Snowdrifts shelter the walls, but Frostmane trolls and wild beasts prowl the frozen valley, keeping the defenders alert. Anvilmar may take its name from High King Modimus Anvilmar. He ruled the dwarven clans before the War of the Three Hammers. Today, the garrison keeps watch and tends the forge fires as trolls and beasts roam the valley.

subzone:astranaar.text: Astranaar. Across its island in central Ashenvale, Astranaar offers refuge to Alliance travelers as threats gather in the forest. The old forest road runs beside the settlement, where furbolgs, satyrs, and the Horde endanger the Night Elves’ hold. Wooden footbridges lead from Astranaar’s island to the mainland across the forest lake. This is Ashenvale’s largest night elven settlement, where sentinels, priests, and artisans watch over the woodland. Travelers can find an inn, traders, and an expert leatherworker. From the high perches, a flight master sends hippogryphs to distant outposts across Kalimdor. Lanterns shine over Astranaar’s quiet waters, yet the town stays ready for attack. Raene Wolfrunner and other local leaders direct patrols and defenses against the corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs advancing from the north. The Sentinels fear the furbolgs may assault the settlement.

subzone:auberdine.text: Auberdine. Ships crowd Auberdine's docks, carrying travelers between Darkshore, Teldrassil, and the Eastern Kingdoms. The night elven town is the Alliance's main port in northern Kalimdor, between the Veiled Sea and pine-covered bluffs. Auberdine stands on the Veiled Sea, the only major settlement still thriving in Darkshore. Ships sail to Stormwind Harbor and, by way of Southshore, to Menethil Harbor. Ferries cross to Rut'theran Village beneath the boughs of the World Tree. Unlike Teldrassil's secluded treetop cities, Auberdine welcomes travelers from across the sea. Lamps light its stone streets, where dwarves and gnomes mingle with merchants among low, arched timber houses. Elder Thundris Windweaver and the Auberdine Village Council govern the town. They coordinate Darkshore's defense with the local Sentinels. Auberdine is a vital trade hub, though Darnassus rarely speaks its name; memory there dwells on the great cities lost to the Sundering. Trouble presses from every side. Aggressive murlocs raid fishing boats along the strand, corrupted Blackwood furbolgs push from the south, and foul magic drifting down from Felwood agitates the wildlife.

subzone:azurelode-mine.text: Azurelode Mine. Southshore's militia guards the human laborers at Azurelode Mine, whose iron feeds the Alliance war effort in southwestern Hillsbrad. Just west of Southshore, Azurelode Mine cuts into the coastal ridges, beyond the open farmland. Human miners work deep underground under Foreman Bonds's watch, drawing iron for arms and armor. That iron helps Alliance defenders hold the region against the Undercity. Southshore's garrisons and town militia rely on Azurelode Mine for most of their raw iron. So Tarren Mill targets the workers and guards, seeking to break the supply lines that sustain Hillsbrad's human strongholds.

subzone:ban-ethil-barrow-den.text: Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Beneath Teldrassil's roots, Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The sacred chambers were made for the sleeping Druids of the Talon, whose spirits commune with the Emerald Dream. Now the den is a dangerous warren, and the druids within are at risk. Ban'ethil Barrow Den lies beneath Teldrassil's roots, with chambers above and below. Barrow dens shelter night elf druids as they sleep and send their spirits into the Emerald Dream. This den was made for the Druids of the Talon to commune with nature. Its halls once held quiet meditation, but corruption spreading through Teldrassil's wildlife reached the Gnarlpine furbolgs. They invaded and made the hollowed chambers a fortified warren. The Gnarlpine tribe has gone mad under a mysterious corruption spreading across the World Tree. Its furbolgs drove out or endangered the sleeping druids, and now guard the winding tunnels fiercely. Any night elf who approaches is attacked. Teldrassil's defenders must drive the furbolgs back to protect the vulnerable druids and the sacred relics trapped in the den's lower depths.

subzone:ban-ethil-hollow.text:
Ban'ethil Hollow. Furbolgs threaten travelers in Ban'ethil Hollow, south of the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus. At the ravine's far end, a hidden entrance leads to Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Furbolgs roam the rocky descent into Ban'ethil Hollow. A strange affliction has driven them mad, and they stalk the nearby road to ambush couriers and wandering sentinels. The hollow lies just south of the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus. Here, Teldrassil's woods are not wholly safe.

At the ravine's back stands the entrance to Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Slumbering druids and ancient tunnels lie within, threatened by the maddened beasts outside.

subzone:baradin-bay.text: Baradin Bay. Baradin Bay's reefs and wrecks make every crossing perilous. The waters lie between Khaz Modan, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, and southern Lordaeron. During the Second War, Kul Tiras patrolled the bay with a powerful navy. Baradin Bay joins the harbors of the Eastern Kingdoms. Menethil Harbor stands on the Wetlands shore, while Southshore lies in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Sandbanks and jagged shoals hide beneath the water. Murlocs, crocolisks, and deep-sea sharks make the passage more dangerous. Kul Tiras and the Horde fought across Baradin Bay during the Second War. Along the Wetlands coast, the broken hulls of the Kul Tiran Third Fleet lie half-submerged. They are known as the Lost Fleet. Other ships sank at Drowned Reef. Hostile spirits, salvagers, and sea beasts haunt the waters around the ruined ships.

subzone:bashal-aran.text:
Bashal'Aran. In northern Darkshore, Bashal'Aran's ruins draw satyrs and grells to lingering magic. A lone elven ghost remains bound by a curse centuries old. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne in Bashal'Aran and its twin, Ameth'Aran. The mage Athrikus Narassin governed both towns. Their splendid markets and temples honored Elune.

When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the cataclysm destroyed both settlements. For reasons lost to time, Athrikus used his arcane mastery to bind his second-in-command, the mage Asterion, inside a moonstone seal in Bashal'Aran. Asterion's body perished, but his ghost remained shackled to the ruined shrine. Deth'ryll satyrs and grells claim Bashal'Aran's crumbled stones. Drawn by magic lingering in the ancient masonry, they feed on its energy to strengthen their foul arts. They swarm the broken courtyards and terrorize travelers on Darkshore's forest paths.

Yet the creatures keep clear of the central shrine, where Asterion endures his endless vigil.

subzone:bathran-s-haunt.text: Bathran's Haunt. Forsaken herbalists harvest rare plants at Bathran's Haunt, east of the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. Their work is withering the woodland around the ancient kaldorei ruin. Crumbling night elf pillars rise north of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran, caught in Ashenvale's thick foliage. Once a tranquil kaldorei relic, Bathran's Haunt now shelters Forsaken herbalists and their enforcers. They work among broken marble in an open-air laboratory, gathering rare woodland reagents for experiments. As they harvest, grass rots brown and blossoms wilt. Decay creeps through the grove, blighting the ancient soil. Bathran's Hair grows only among these stones, and it is a unique remedial herb. Night elf and Alliance scouts see its harvest as desecration of sacred elven soil. Forsaken herbalists seek the plant's potent properties, and the Horde has an interest in its yield. Yet the Forsaken keep their methods secret. The corrupted earth draws suspicion from outsiders and allies alike.

subzone:beggar-s-haunt.text: Beggar's Haunt. Forsaken agents watch the eastern approaches from Beggar's Haunt, an old Stormwind tower. It stands on a hillside in northeastern Duskwood, near the mountain road to Deadwind Pass. Beggar's Haunt looks over the hills east of Manor Mistmantle. Stormwind once kept guards here to watch the kingdom's eastern approaches. As Duskwood sank into gloom, the patrols withdrew to Darkshire and left the tower to weather and ruin. Now Forsaken agents study the region from within Alliance territory. Among them are members of the Royal Apothecary Society and the Deathstalkers. A winding path behind Beggar's Haunt descends to Knight's Hollow, where a secluded pool lies beneath a waterfall. An unmarked grave rests between two hooded stone statues, like the guardians beside the Dark Portal. Nearby graves include the resting place of an Unknown Soldier. These graves recall forgotten clashes along the frontier, fought long before the Forsaken took the watchtower.

subzone:blackwolf-river.text: Blackwolf River. Through Windshear Crag, Blackwolf River carries runoff from the Venture Company's logging and industrial work. Its waters flow down from Cragpool Lake. Fed by Cragpool Lake, Blackwolf River runs through Windshear Crag. Venture Company loggers cut the surrounding woods with heavy machinery and buzzsaws. Sludge, oil, and logging waste drain into the current, carrying the cost of the company's work through the basin.

subzone:blackwood-den.text: Blackwood Den. In southern Darkshore, Blackwood Den has fallen to the Blackwood furbolgs’ corruption. Their cave and camps, once a peaceful home near Ashenvale, now echo with madness. Volcor, a night elf scout, is trapped inside and awaits aid from Auberdine. Near the southern border of Darkshore and Ashenvale, Blackwood furbolgs hold a rocky cave and crude camps. Corruption has taken hold of the tribe, and its members attack outsiders. Deep inside the cave, the night elf Volcor is pinned down and in danger. Scouts and travelers from Auberdine are needed to help him.

subzone:bloodtooth-camp.text: Bloodtooth Camp. In central Ashenvale, Bloodtooth Camp lies west of the Falfarren River. Ran Bloodtooth leads the corrupted furbolgs, who attack anyone approaching. Alliance scouts seek to cleanse the surrounding woodlands. Bloodtooth Camp lies southwest of the southern Moonwell and west of the Falfarren River. The furbolgs were once bound to Kalimdor’s sacred wilderness, but lingering spiritual corruption has consumed their tribe. Ran Bloodtooth commands the crude settlement. His followers attack travelers and night elven protectors alike.

subzone:bough-shadow.text: Bough Shadow. In northeastern Ashenvale, Bough Shadow lies east of Forest Song beneath a colossal Great Tree. Its roots surround an ancient portal into the Emerald Dream. At Bough Shadow, the Great Tree’s roots wind around a natural crossing into the Emerald Dream. The Green Dragonflight guards the quiet grove. Emerald drakes such as Phantim and Dreamstalker circle above the canopy. Emeraldon dragonspawn and oracles patrol the swirling green portal at the tree’s base. Mortals who approach without permission are turned away.

subzone:boulderslide-cavern.text: Boulderslide Cavern. Boulderslide kobolds dig deep in Boulderslide Cavern, at the far end of Boulderslide Ravine. They search the stone for glowing mineral formations. Boulderslide kobolds have carved a stronghold into the Stonetalon crags. They dig frantically for resonite, a rare purple crystal embedded in the stone. Its glow carries traces of earthen magic, and the kobolds turn fiercely against anyone who approaches their excavation.

subzone:boulderslide-ravine.text: Boulderslide Ravine. Along Webwinder Path, Boulderslide Ravine cuts through the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains. Horde and Alliance fighting rarely reaches this quiet pass. Rocky slopes lead toward Boulderslide Cavern, while wild mountain beasts roam the heights. Webwinder Path leads into Boulderslide Ravine, high in the Stonetalon Mountains. Loggers, night elves, and the Horde fight over timber and sacred glades elsewhere in the region, but soldiers rarely enter this narrow pass. Mountain rams and crag beasts roam its ledges and sheer walls. Cliff Stormers are among them. Prospectors watch the slopes for rich mineral veins on the way toward the deeper cavern network. Across from Boulderslide Cavern's entrance, a small cave looks over the ravine. Rough torches light weathered supply barrels and primitive tribal paintings. The designs resemble ancient tauren art. They suggest native tribes once traveled through these crags or took shelter here, long before modern conflict reached the mountains.

subzone:brackwell-pumpkin-patch.text: Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. Defias brigands hold Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in southeastern Elwynn Forest. The farm belonged to the Brackwell family, but now conspirators meet in its cottage and fields, where stolen mine gold arrives. Southeast of the Stonefield homestead, Brackwell's fields lie untended. The family vanished as crime spread through the area, driven away or worse. The Defias Brotherhood now occupies the sturdy cottage and overgrown fields. Beyond the reach of Goldshire's patrols, brigands regroup here. Morgan the Collector and other prominent conspirators use the isolated farm to receive illicit gold from the forest's mines.

subzone:brewnall-village.text: Brewnall Village. In Chill Breeze Valley, the Barleybrew family works on new brews and guards against wild beasts. Their camp lies near the entrance to Gnomeregan. The Barleybrew clan brews in Chill Breeze Valley, among the gnomish reaches of western Dun Morogh. They work to perfect old recipes and make the finest stout. Tents and brewing gear fill the camp, with no permanent stone buildings. As the Barleybrews test new ales, wolves and bears threaten the valley. Wandering mountaineers gather rare ingredients and help keep the area safe.

subzone:brightwood-grove.text: Brightwood Grove. West of Darkshire, ruined farms and overgrown clearings shelter savage Nightbane worgen in Brightwood Grove. Brightwood Grove lies within sight of Darkshire, where ruined farms and fences mark the town's edge. Nightbane worgen make crude camps among the overgrown clearings and prowl close to town. Their presence threatens Darkshire. So the Night Watch and travelers passing through keep their numbers down to protect the settlement.

subzone:calmbreeze-inn.text:
Calmbreeze Inn. In Shen'dar Village and Valaanar, Calmbreeze Inns offer travelers rest on Zephras Isle. Both provide shelter and local services. Travelers can rest at the Calmbreeze Inns on Zephras Isle. Coriella Calmbreeze runs the inn in Shen'dar Village, where island tradesfolk gather. There, you can find mentors in herbalism, skinning, and enchanting.

Across the way, the Valaanar inn welcomes local wayfarers and shelters rare curios. Upstairs, an audio crystal holds a recording of the ancient rebellion in Eldre'Thalas.

subzone:camp-aparaje.text: Camp Aparaje. Grimtotem warriors now hold Camp Aparaje in the eastern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. They slaughtered the peaceful tauren who settled there and claimed the outpost. Peaceful tauren once made their home among the Stonetalon crags, seeking a quiet life in the highlands. Then raiders from nearby Grimtotem Post struck under Grundig Darkcloud's lead. The attackers butchered some villagers and drove others away. Survivors such as Makaba Flathoof mourn their lost home and fear for kin taken captive. Grimtotem warriors now occupy Camp Aparaje as a forward base for their aggressive tribe in the region. Many Grimtotem settlements bear blue markings, but the great totem here is painted deep crimson.

subzone:canals-stormwind-city.text: Canals (Stormwind City). Walkers and anglers share the paths beside Stormwind's Canals, winding between the city's districts. You can follow the Canals from the Trade District's markets to Old Town's aged alleys, the cathedral gardens, and the Dwarven District. Stone bridges and archways cross the water, while paths pass the Gallina Winery, tailor shops, and quiet homes. Merchants and fishermen use these waterways. Beneath the streets, the fortified Stockade entrance holds Stormwind's most dangerous criminals and rebels. The Horde sacked Stormwind during the First War, leaving the Canals in ruins. The waterways were restored as the capital rose again after the Second War. Now they are clean and repaired, though rumors speak of a massive albino crocolisk beneath the docks.

subzone:cathedral-of-light.text:
Cathedral of Light. In Cathedral Square, the Cathedral of Light is the Church of the Holy Light’s chief sanctuary. It is Stormwind’s spiritual heart and the center of human priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Archbishop Benedictus leads the faithful from the Cathedral of Light, rebuilt after the First War’s devastation. Archbishop Alonsus Faol and Bishop Benedictus guided its restoration. Its towering form still recalls the city’s resilience.

After the Scourge took Lordaeron during the Third War, the Church moved its seat south to Stormwind. From the great hall, Benedictus gives spiritual guidance to the Alliance. The Cathedral of Light is a place of prayer and healing. It is also the Knights of the Silver Hand’s main headquarters in the southern kingdoms.

Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker and Duthorian Rall train promising squires in the sacred trials of the Tome of Valor and the Tome of Divinity. High Priestess Laurena teaches acolytes the deepest tenets of the Light. She prepares holy champions to defend the realm from the growing threats of the Defias Brotherhood and the Scourge.

subzone:cathedral-square.text: Cathedral Square. In Cathedral Square, faith and civic life gather beneath the Cathedral of Light. City Hall, the orphanage, and the Argent Dawn's Stormwind headquarters are here. Northwest of the Trade District and southeast of the Dwarven District, Cathedral Square draws the faithful from across the Kingdom of Stormwind. The Cathedral of Light rises above the square, foremost sanctuary of the Holy Light across Azeroth. Priests, paladins, and healers come to study, pray, and train. Citizens and pilgrims mingle with schoolchildren led by School Mistress Danna. Prayer shares Cathedral Square with the kingdom's work. City Hall and the Stormwind Orphanage anchor its civic life. Along the avenues, armorers and weaponsmiths serve holy crusaders, including Righteous Plates and Just Maces. The Argent Dawn keeps its Stormwind base here. Its recruiters and representatives coordinate relief and rally champions against the Scourge in the northern kingdoms.

subzone:cenarion-enclave.text:
Cenarion Enclave. In Darnassus, the Cenarion Circle gathers beneath Fandral Staghelm's leadership of the night elven druids. The Cenarion Enclave is their meeting place and seat of power, set among the capital's great hollows and living boughs. High above the Temple Gardens, the Cenarion Enclave brings the Cenarion Circle together beneath ancient oaks and ashes whose bark bears runes. Its halls are shaped from living wood and stone. With Malfurion Stormrage absent in the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm oversees the Circle's affairs here. His ambitious vision for Teldrassil meets political friction with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind.

Druids meditate beside the streams, and the capital's hunters gather here as well. At the stables, skilled riders learn to tame Darnassian nightsabers. Known as a tranquil sanctuary, the Cenarion Enclave also shelters quiet work beneath its westernmost bough. Under the hollowed roots lies a refuge where Darnassus's clandestine rogues work, shielded by the canopy above.

subzone:champions-hall.text: Champions' Hall. In Stormwind's guarded Champions' Hall, Alliance officers gather to discuss campaigns across Azeroth. Its quartermasters supply proven veterans with specialized weapons, plate, and regalia. Only Alliance soldiers who have earned the rank of Knight or higher in battle pass the guarded entrance to Champions' Hall. Commanders gather around maps of Azeroth to discuss ongoing campaigns, among arms and the insignias of rank. Quartermasters supply battle-hardened soldiers with elite weapons and armor to aid them against the Horde in contested lands, along with mounts.

subzone:charred-vale.text:
Charred Vale. In southwestern Stonetalon, fire and smoke still consume the Charred Vale. The Venture Company's logging left the woodland in ruins, and fire elementals roam while Bloodfury harpies defend their territory. Once, trees filled the basin in southwestern Stonetalon, and treants guarded the woodland. Native chimaeras and harpies lived among them. Then the Venture Company's goblins arrived with explosive machinery and cut down the forest. Their work corrupted the treants and woke chaotic fire elementals.

The treants drove the goblins back, but the loggers left a broken land scarred by fire. Whatever foul devices they used as they fled also tainted the valley. Blackened ancients wander blindly through smoke and ash, while enraged elementals roam nearby. Bloodfury harpies roost in skeletal snags and defend what remains of their territory.

Druids from Sun Rock Retreat will not abandon the valley. They send travelers to sow enchanted seeds and tend the corrupted ancients as they work to reclaim the scorched earth.

subzone:chill-breeze-valley.text:
Chill Breeze Valley. In western Dun Morogh, travelers cross Chill Breeze Valley between Kharanos and Gnomeregan. Refugees and young travelers follow the main trail, while dangerous beasts haunt the secluded reaches. A T-shaped trench cuts through the mountains, its main trail running east to west. Young dwarves and gnomes travel between Kharanos and the outskirts of Gnomeregan. The north-south branch leads into dangerous ground. Blood stains the snow, and mangled carcasses lie nearby.

Savage wendigos make dens in deep ice caves. They prey on anyone who wanders into their hunting grounds.

subzone:clean-zone.text: Clean Zone. Gnomes hold the Clean Zone as a refuge inside ruined Gnomeregan. Beyond the upper Hall of Gears, this fortified enclave stays safe amid the irradiated city. Medics, technicians, and Sparklematic machines support its defenders and salvage work. The Clean Zone remains untainted while most of Gnomeregan fell to Mekkatorque's disastrous venting of radioactive waste. It lies between the trogg-infested Dormitory below and the contested Hall of Gears above. Gnome defenders, technicians, and field medics hold its barricades day and night. Alliance expeditions regroup here, tend wounds, and maintain their machinery. The Clean Zone also supports salvage from Gnomeregan's ruined capital. Gnomish engineers installed Sparklematic 5200 units to scrub and wash grime-encrusted relics brought up from the city's radioactive depths. Technicians and merchants such as Tink Sprocketwhistle process reclaimed gears and baubles, outfit adventurers, and study the toxic fallout in the deep tunnels.

subzone:cleft.text: Cleft. Northwest of Dolanaar, Gnarlpine furbolgs ambush travelers in the Cleft. Off the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus, Gnarlpine furbolgs have made their den in the Cleft. Teldrassil’s spreading corruption has driven them mad, and they have fortified the hollow. From there, they threaten travelers on the main road and may cut Dolanaar off from Darnassus.

subzone:cliffspring-falls.text:
Cliffspring Falls. At Cliffspring Falls, water pours from Darkshore’s eastern cliffs into the forest below. The falls feed the Cliffspring River and once supplied nearby night elf settlements. Now a foul taint spreads through the river basin. Cliffspring Falls rises from caves high in Darkshore’s eastern bluffs and feeds the Cliffspring River. The river winds west through the woods before emptying into the sea. Its clear waters once gave nearby night elf settlements their purest drinking water.

Now the water runs murky and foul, carrying sickness and decay through the river basin. Naturalists who investigate the falls find naga and cultists overrunning the caves. They plot in the shadows as demonic corruption from neighboring Felwood threatens to seep through the highland bedrock.

subzone:coldridge-pass.text: Coldridge Pass. Troggs now bar the road through Coldridge Pass, the way out of Coldridge Valley. Recruits leave Coldridge Valley through Coldridge Pass and travel toward Kharanos. The tunnel cuts through Dun Morogh’s southern mountain ridge, carrying them from sheltered training grounds into the wider kingdom. Troggs have overrun the passage, threatening anyone who crosses between the valley and the rest of Dun Morogh.

subzone:command-center.text: Command Center. Stormwind's army is thinned by campaigns abroad, and recruits drill in the Command Center. Also called the Stormwind Barracks, it houses the city's officers and a seasoned crew focused on training recruits and local militia. In Old Town, Stormwind's Command Center trains the kingdom's soldiers. Much of the royal army serves abroad, leaving its halls quieter than usual. Veteran instructors Ander Germaine and martial artist Wu Shen drill fresh warriors to strengthen the city's defenses. When you seek instruction in heavy arms or tactical combat, Stormwind's guards may direct you to the Barracks. It stands near the Pig and Whistle Tavern and Old Town's shadowy operations. The training ground helps keep order in a district known for tavern brawls and roguish activity.

subzone:commons.text: Commons. Travelers and traders fill the Commons just inside Ironforge's gates. From here, the mountain city's great caverns open before them, and merchants, travelers, and bankers arrive from across the Alliance. The Commons greets you just northeast of the Gates of Ironforge. Its market street is cut from mountain stone, with the Alliance Auction House, Stonefire Tavern, and the central bank in the Vault of Ironforge. Broad roads lead to the Great Forge, the Mystic Ward, and the Military Ward. Nearly everyone crossing the city passes its shops. Trade reaches the Commons from across the Eastern Kingdoms. Ironforge's central position and the underground Deeprun Tram to Stormwind bring travelers and merchants through its streets. Adventurers trade goods from across Azeroth, buy weapons at Steelfury's Weapon Emporium, or purchase reagents from Barim. Some gather beneath the inn's warm lanterns before setting out into the snows of Khaz Modan.

subzone:craftsmen-s-terrace.text: Craftsmen's Terrace. Workshops and visitors gather along Darnassus's northern edge at Craftsmen's Terrace. Its trainers, inn, and Argent Dawn embassy serve artisans and travelers. Woodworkers, leathercrafters, alchemists, and other artisans work along Darnassus's northern edge. Their shops gather the trades that keep the city running, with night elven methods put to practical use. An inn, a guild master, and guild petition vendors serve visitors here. Bridges lead west to the Cenarion Enclave and south to the Warrior's Terrace. The Argent Dawn keeps an embassy in the Craftsmen's Terrace and coordinates with northern allies against the Scourge. Scattered scholarly volumes rest among the workshops. They include histories of the War of the Ancients, chronicles of the Second War, and treatises on the Old Gods.

subzone:cragpool-lake.text: Cragpool Lake. In Windshear Crag, the Venture Company’s timberworks hang above Cragpool Lake and its dark water. At Cragpool Lake, Venture Company platforms cross above the water beneath a vast timber structure. Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle watches operations across the mountain valley. Company workers occupy the platforms overhead.

subzone:crystal-lake.text: Crystal Lake. At Crystal Lake, murlocs claim the shore east of Goldshire. Their attacks endanger villagers and travelers passing by. East of Goldshire, Crystal Lake lies within walking distance of the Lion's Pride Inn. Freshwater murlocs claim its shore and shallow shoals, attacking anyone who comes too close. William Pestle, an alchemist at the inn, hires travelers to drive them back and gather the crystal kelp they carry for his experiments.

subzone:cut-throat-alley.text:
Cut-Throat Alley. In Cut-Throat Alley, a hidden courtyard lies beyond a canal shop in Stormwind City. Its paved path ends at an empty residence, out of sight of ordinary city traffic. Step through the Shady Lady and a paved dead end opens before you. Stacked crates and forgotten barrels sit beside a two-story residence with no one at home. Though the alley is counted within the Dwarven District, it lies apart from the district's forge fires and soot.

No main avenue reaches Cut-Throat Alley. Its only footpath passes through the canal-side shop, just south of the bridge from Cathedral Square. Passing guards and ordinary citizens cannot see this quiet corner of the capital.

subzone:dagger-hills.text: Dagger Hills. Bandits hold Dagger Hills, the rocky heights behind Moonbrook in southern Westfall. With royal patrols gone, the ridge threatens travelers and the plains below. The Defias Brotherhood uses this dry highland as a stronghold. Knuckledusters, pathstalkers and highwaymen hide among the crests and scrub. They ambush unwary travelers and watch the approaches to their strongholds below, keeping the surrounding plains under threat. Darkness brings danger to Dagger Hills. After sunset, Leprithus, a wandering ghoul, has been seen stalking the desolate heights. Outlaws and lingering undead roam the ridge. Nearby, Grimbooze Thunderbrew, a dwarven brewer, sets up his distilling equipment despite the dangers.

subzone:darkcloud-pinnacle.text: Darkcloud Pinnacle. Grimtotem tauren hold Darkcloud Pinnacle above the canyon east of the Great Lift. From their linked mesas, they disrupt the region and pursue secret dealings. Darkcloud Pinnacle rises above the canyon basin across three main mesas, joined by rope bridges. You can climb a steep natural slope from the canyon floor, then cross wooden bridges. A high crossing near Razorfen Downs offers another way up. From these windswept rocks, Grimtotem watchers survey the valley. The heights guard them from easy attack and leave them apart from the wider tauren tribes.

subzone:darkened-bank.text: Darkened Bank. At Duskwood’s northern edge, Darkened Bank runs beside Elwynn Forest. Its shore reaches east toward the Redridge Mountains, between safer ground and the forest’s terrors. Darkened Bank follows the river that divides Duskwood from Elwynn Forest. Its shore stretches from the western bends to the stone span leading to the Redridge Mountains. Beneath Duskwood’s gloomy canopy, travelers coming south from Elwynn often reach this ground first. Near the western tip, a makeshift camp shelters the displaced Sven Yorgen and Lars, just beyond the deep woods.

subzone:darkshire.text:
Darkshire. Darkshire's Night Watch holds the line while Duskwood's unnatural gloom closes around the town. With little aid from Stormwind, the people must guard their homes. Darkshire began as Grand Hamlet, a peaceful woodland settlement. The Old Horde razed it during the First War, and the village rose again. After Medivh fell at Karazhan, the death throes left in the surrounding woods made them the shadowed wilderness of Duskwood.

Darkshire belongs to the Kingdom of Stormwind, yet the crown sends virtually no aid to its town hall. Political paralysis in Stormwind City has left the garrison unstaffed and the borders unpatrolled. Mayor Ello Ebonlocke and the local council govern alone, enforcing harsh, insular justice in the shadows. Walking dead from the western graveyards and feral worgen in the woods press against Darkshire's palisades. The Night Watch, a voluntary civilian militia led by Althea Ebonlocke, is the town's chief defense. From the town square, weary sentries patrol the pitch-black roads, keep them open, and turn back terrors at the tree line.

At the Scarlet Raven Tavern, travelers meet locals who are suspicious, frightened, and desperate for anyone able to wield a blade.

subzone:darkshire-town-hall.text:
Darkshire Town Hall. In Darkshire Town Hall, the mayor and council govern a town besieged by darkness and undead. Its dim halls are the seat of their rule. Just west of Darkshire's main square, the Town Hall is where the town's leaders govern an increasingly isolated territory. Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke struggles to keep order and protect the people while Stormwind sends little military aid.

Clerk Daltry and other officials track town records and the travelers who brave Duskwood's dangerous roads. With danger all around, keeping those ledgers current is grim work.

subzone:dawning-wood-catacombs.text:
Dawning Wood Catacombs. Beneath Raven Hill Cemetery in western Duskwood, undead fill the Dawning Wood Catacombs. Skeletal guards and ravenous ghouls haunt their stone tunnels. Beneath the ruined Raven Hill Cemetery, the Dawning Wood Catacombs hold the dead of the surrounding woods. Before twilight cursed the forest, those dead rested in these stone corridors. Now the catacombs shelter some of the region’s deadliest undead, and lone travelers face danger in their depths.

Two underground wings divide the catacombs. Animated skeletons guard ancestral tombs in the western passages. To the east, tunnels descend into a foul warren overrun by ravenous, disease-bearing ghouls.

subzone:dead-acre.text: Dead Acre. In southeastern Westfall, Dead Acre lies burned and abandoned near the bridge to Duskwood. The Defias Brotherhood torched the farm during its uprising, and rogue harvest golems still stalk the blackened fields. North of the road from Sentinel Hill to Duskwood, Dead Acre stands among Westfall’s old breadbasket farms. The homestead once gave good harvests, until the Defias Brotherhood rose in revolt and drove out the landowners. Then farm and crops went up in flames. Scorched timber and smoking earth remain, while mechanical Harvest Watchers still reap the barren soil.

subzone:deeprun-tram.text:
Deeprun Tram. Beneath the mountains, the Deeprun Tram carries travelers between Ironforge and Stormwind City. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned it after the Second War, and its twin tracks carry citizens, soldiers, and goods between the Alliance capitals. After the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard sought a faster way to send dwarven aid and supplies to Stormwind. Mountain passes made the journey slow, so he asked High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to design an underground railway.

Gnomish engineers cut a route beneath a mountain and through a vast subterranean lake. Rats plagued the work, but the tram was finished. It carries thousands between Ironforge and Stormwind without charge.

subzone:deepwater-tavern.text:
Deepwater Tavern. At Menethil Harbor, the Deepwater Tavern gives travelers a place to rest and seek work. Sailors and adventurers meet there, and harbor rumors may end in a brawl. In Menethil Harbor, the Deepwater Tavern offers shelter from the marsh rain and rough roads. Sailors, dockworkers, merchants, and weary adventurers gather beneath its timber beams. They trade news, meet, warm themselves, and tend their wounds.

Local merchants and a first aid trainer help those bound for the marsh or setting out across the Great Sea. The tavern stays lively, and spilled ale can turn a dispute into a brawl. Tapoke 'Slim' Jahn is known to spark them.

subzone:defias-hideout.text: Defias Hideout. Vagrants and Defias thugs linger in the ruined house on Moonbrook’s southern edge. Its upper floor conceals a route into chambers beneath the town.

subzone:demon-fall-canyon.text:
Demon Fall Canyon. In southern Ashenvale, the canyon bears the scars of the battle that freed the orcs from the blood curse. Thrall and Grommash Hellscream faced Mannoroth here. Near Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Ridge, the canyon still bears the scars of the Third War. Warchief Thrall and chieftain Grommash Hellscream tracked the pit lord Mannoroth here to break his hold over the Horde. Mannoroth struck Thrall down. Grom seized the chance to drive his axe, Gorehowl, into the demon’s chest.

The infernal blast shattered Mannoroth and killed Grom. With the pit lord’s death, the orcs were free of their lingering demonic servitude. The Horde named the canyon for Grom’s final stand and raised a monument nearby to honor his redemption. Mannoroth’s death unleashed demonic power that tainted the surrounding land. Fel magic still saturates the canyon, where lesser demons roam. Pilgrims who come to this hallowed ground face danger at every turn.

subzone:demon-fall-ridge.text: Demon Fall Ridge. Demons hold Demon Fall Ridge in southeastern Ashenvale, above the place where Mannoroth fell. Fel magic still stains the heights, and the Burning Legion has claimed a night elf barrow den. West of Demon Fall Canyon, Demon Fall Ridge looks down on the place where Grommash Hellscream fought the pit lord Mannoroth. Its cliffs still bear the fel scars of the Third War. The demons who survived use the heights as a staging ground. Lesser demons patrol the rocky slopes, defile the woodland, and threaten travelers along Ashenvale’s southern border. A night elf barrow den lies abandoned in the ridge’s side. Dark sorcery now fills the passages where druids once slept. Fel fiends prowl its halls, and deep within, Diathorus the Seeker rules the conclave. The cunning dreadlord directs the demons who remain across the forest.

subzone:demont-s-place.text: Demont's Place. Outlaws hold Demont's Place, west of Moonbrook in southwestern Westfall. Once its fields fed the Kingdom of Stormwind. Economic collapse and the Defias Brotherhood drove the caretakers away, leaving the fields empty and the fences weathered. Demont's Place lies within sight of Moonbrook, among the family holdings that once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind. Economic collapse and outlaw brigands stripped the farm of its livelihood and drove its caretakers away. Now outlaws use its grounds as an extension of the Defias stronghold in Moonbrook. The Defias Brotherhood holds Demont's Place on the outskirts of Moonbrook. Thugs, cutpurses, and displaced laborers linger among its fences and shattered buildings. They ambush travelers who stray from the southern roads. Until Moonbrook is reclaimed and the outlaws are broken, peaceful farming cannot return.

subzone:dolanaar.text: Dolanaar. At Dolanaar, travelers and guides gather beneath Teldrassil’s boughs. Southwest of Shadowglen, the town is the first place young night elves reach after leaving their sheltered training grounds. Rangers, druids, and craftsmen help newcomers as strange afflictions spread through the World Tree. Beneath Teldrassil’s canopy, Dolanaar is a crossroads for travelers. Southwest of Shadowglen, its homes and platforms follow the traditional night elven way, woven into the woodland. Young night elves come here for their first broad training in trades, martial arts, and nature crafts. The road west leads toward Darnassus, the capital. Reports of corrupted wildlife, aggressive furbolgs, and foul mosses come from the surrounding boughs, and Dolanaar’s council hears them.

subzone:dor-danil-barrow-den.text:
Dor'Danil Barrow Den. South of Splintertree Post, Dor'Danil Barrow Den lies under Forsaken shadow. Druids once slept here while their spirits roamed the Emerald Dream. Now horror fills the sanctuary. For centuries, night elven druids have slept in barrow dens across Kalimdor. Their bodies rest underground while their spirits travel the Emerald Dream. When the Horde pushed into Ashenvale, Dor'Danil lay deep behind enemy lines. The orcs mostly left the sleeping elves alone, but the newly allied Forsaken saw an opportunity. Their agents entered the depths and began experiments to sever the druids from their spirits.

The ordeal fractured the dreamers' minds and drove them mad. Now sinister Forsaken assassins prowl the dark hollows. The tormented spirits of druids who cannot return to their bodies haunt them too.

subzone:dormitory.text: Dormitory. In Gnomeregan, troggs now overrun the Dormitory, and radiation chokes its halls. Gnomes once made their homes here, but the creatures that drove them out now hold the fallen city's residential quarters. Beyond the Clean Zone's decontamination chambers, the Dormitory once housed Gnomeregan's inventors, laborers, and families. When High Tinker Mekkatorque opened the emergency radiation vents to fight the invading troggs, this crowded part of the city became a trap. No gnomish life remains in its communal halls or living quarters. Mutated troggs thrive in the radioactive air. To reach the lower Hall of Gears, travelers must fight through this reminder of the catastrophe. Though the living quarters are abandoned, Gnomeregan's administrative machines still work. Matrix Punchograph 3005-B terminals process security punch cards. The cards open higher-security data terminals deeper in the city, where important records remain from the gnomes' flight.

subzone:dun-algaz.text: Dun Algaz. Dragonmaw orcs have seized Dun Algaz, closing the easy road between Ironforge's lands and Menethil Harbor. Its guarded pass and tunnels join Loch Modan to the Wetlands. Dun Algaz cuts through the jagged peaks between Loch Modan and the Wetlands. The pass was already there before the War of the Three Hammers. After the Wildhammer clan was driven from Ironforge, its people traveled this way north. Stone tunnels, bastions, and watchposts guard the road. Whoever holds Dun Algaz commands the only overland route from the dwarven heartlands to Menethil Harbor on the western sea. After their defeat at Dun Modr in the Second War, the Old Horde retreated to Dun Algaz. The pass became their last southern bulwark against Sir Anduin Lothar's forces. The Alliance took it back for a time, but Dragonmaw orcs have overrun the stronghold again. Dwarven Mountaineers have withdrawn to the upper tunnels, leaving a deadly gauntlet for travelers through the mountain corridor.

subzone:dun-garok.text: Dun Garok. Dun Garok holds the southeastern heights of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Captain Ironhill leads its dwarven garrison, defending Alliance interests and nearby operations at the Azurelode Mine. The Forsaken of Tarren Mill see the stronghold as a threat on their border. Dun Garok holds the crags in southeastern Hillsbrad. Captain Ironhill leads the Ironforge mountaineers and riflemen who defend the outpost. They guard human settlements and protect Alliance operations at the Azurelode Mine. Stone walls and deep entrenchments help the garrison withstand nearby threats. Dun Garok lies close to Tarren Mill, and the Forsaken see it as an intrusion on their southern border. Sylvanas Windrunner's forces resent the armed dwarves near their stronghold. They plot to enter the fortress, break its defenses, and kill Captain Ironhill's garrison to secure Forsaken control of Hillsbrad.

subzone:dun-modr.text:
Dun Modr. Dark Iron dwarves hold Dun Modr and the southern approach to the Thandol Span. The fortress changed hands in a fierce struggle during the Second War. At Wetlands' northern edge, Dun Modr guards the main road between Khaz Modan and the northern human kingdoms. Armies have fought for that route across the decades. During the Second War, the Orcish Horde seized the dwarven stronghold and used it to launch raids and resist Alliance armies.

Stromgarde warriors sailed from Tol Barad to reclaim it, but the Orcs struck back in a bloody struggle. At last, Alliance forces under Lord Anduin Lothar drove the invaders south across the Thandol Span and returned the fortress to dwarven hands. With Ironforge's attention divided and many of its finest mountaineers serving the Alliance abroad, Dun Modr lay exposed. Dark Iron invaders took their chance. They sabotaged the Thandol Span with explosives, then swarmed the fortress. Led by the warlock Balgaras the Foul, they overcame the defenders and drove out the Bronzebeard garrison. Now mountaineers hold a grim perimeter just down the road, seeking aid to drive out the occupiers.

subzone:durnholde-keep.text:
Durnholde Keep. Outlaws shelter in Durnholde Keep, east of Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The shattered fortress once served as the Alliance headquarters for the southern orc internment camps. Now the Syndicate holds its ruins. After the Second War, the Alliance made Durnholde Keep its headquarters for the southern internment camps. Lieutenant General Aedelas Blackmoore commanded the fortress and its arena, where orcs fought for sport and profit. Blackmoore raised the orphaned infant Go'el as a slave, named him Thrall, and trained him to fight.

With Taretha Foxton's aid, Thrall escaped captivity and later united the scattered orc clans beneath the new Horde. He returned to Durnholde, besieged the keep, and slew Blackmoore. Then he called on the earth spirits to shatter its walls. Durnholde Keep has lain in ruins since its collapse before the Third War. After Lordaeron fell, the Syndicate took refuge among its broken ramparts. The bandits are dispossessed Alterac nobles and cutthroats.

From the ruined bailey and towers, they prey on travelers across the Hillsbrad Foothills. The old fortress now serves them as a fortified outpost.

subzone:dust-plains.text:
Dust Plains. Gnoll packs prowl the Dust Plains, Westfall’s dry southern frontier. The wastes stretch toward the coast and eastern hills, where Klaven’s Tower overlooks the plain. Across southern Westfall, the Dust Plains lead from troubled farmland toward desolate wilderness. Feral gnolls have long claimed this dry ground. They ambush travelers and challenge anyone bound for the coast or nearby hills.

Klaven’s Tower marks the eastern boundary. Klaven Mortwake, a Defias rogue, holds the old mage tower. Gnolls prowl the surrounding wastes, leaving travelers no shelter there.

subzone:dwarven-district.text:
Dwarven District. In Stormwind's northern quarter, Dwarven craftsmen keep their furnaces and workshops at work. The Deeprun Tram links their home to Ironforge. Dwarven artisans, smiths, and engineers make their home in Stormwind's northern quarter. Its heavy stonework, smelting works, and craft shops recall Ironforge. At Potts' Plates, craftspeople from Khaz Modan find familiar company.

On the district's eastern side, an open, arched tunnel leads to the Stormwind station of the Deeprun Tram. The tram links the human capital directly to Ironforge.

subzone:eastvale-logging-camp.text:
Eastvale Logging Camp. Timber orders from Stormwind reach Eastvale Logging Camp, where danger keeps the work from going smoothly. Wolves and bears drive lumberjacks from the eastern woods, but the camp still sends timber to Stormwind and nearby settlements. Timber buyers across the Kingdom of Stormwind send Eastvale Logging Camp orders with strict deadlines. Wolves and bears prowl the woods around the work sites. They drive lumberjacks away and leave cut timber behind.

Supervisor Raelen directs the camp’s work. Travelers help drive off the beasts and recover the abandoned wood before deliveries fall behind schedule. Eastvale Logging Camp has homes and horse stables where travelers can buy fine mounts. On a nearby hill above the work site, retired Marshal Haggard lives in a quiet manor.

He once led the Stormwind Guard. Then he left its service to retire far from the capital’s politics.

subzone:echo-ridge-mine.text: Echo Ridge Mine. Kobolds hold Echo Ridge Mine in the northwestern cliffs of Northshire Valley, where stone and ore once fed the valley. Echo Ridge Mine was cut into the hills above Northshire Abbey to supply the valley with stone and metal. Kobolds poured through its tunnels and drove out the workers. Marshal McBride fears they endanger Northshire's safety and its recruits. So he sends new recruits into the mine to thin their numbers and take it back. Kobolds have pushed beyond Echo Ridge Mine into Elwynn Forest. From the northwestern ridge, they threaten Northshire's training grounds and the flow of resources to the abbey.

subzone:engineering-labs.text: Engineering Labs. In Gnomeregan, the Engineering Labs lie in ruin across tiers linked to the Workshop Entrance and Launch Bay. Once a center of gnome invention, they fell in the city's radioactive catastrophe. Crazed leper gnomes and rogue machines now fill the chambers. The Engineering Labs once held Gnomeregan's work in invention. A central mechanical structure rises through two tiers, joined by a cargo lift. At the city's height, tinkerers made schematics and refined clockwork devices here. Radiation drove the remaining researchers mad. Now deranged leper gnomes guard the malfunctioning machinery beside rogue constructs. The Engineering Labs connect routes through Gnomeregan's lower reaches. Passages lead toward the Launch Bay, Tinkers' Court and the Workshop Entrance back door. On the lower floor, Matrix Punchograph 3005-D terminals process coded punch cards carried by gnome engineers.

subzone:falfarren-river.text:
Falfarren River. The Falfarren River runs through central Ashenvale, dividing night elven lands from Horde outposts. Travelers meet wild dangers and open conflict along its banks. From Mount Hyjal, the Falfarren River spills over waterfalls into Xavian. Then it winds between Splintertree Post and Night Run. In ordinary weather, the water is neither especially deep nor hard to cross.

The river marks a rough boundary through central Ashenvale. Astranaar and the heart of the Kaldorei lands lie west, while Horde camps and lumber operations lie east. Wooden bridges on the main road carry travelers into the contested forest, where patrols clash along the banks. The Falfarren River brings dangers beyond clashes between sentinels and grunts. Near Felfire Hill, corrupted bog beasts and aggressive water creatures prowl the muddy shallows. Rain can swell the currents.

Dense canopies line both shores, where ambushes and skirmishes often spill into the stream.

subzone:fallen-sky-lake.text:
Fallen Sky Lake. At Fallen Sky Lake, Shadethickets defend the shores and central isle between Silverwing Outpost and the Warsong Labor Camp. South of Silverwing Outpost and west of the Warsong Labor Camp, Fallen Sky Lake draws you into contested waters. Hulking Shadethickets roam the shore and the small isle at its center, treating intruders as threats.

A powerful Shadethicket Oracle rules from the isle's heart. The Oracle hoards the fallen moonstones once gathered here and keeps the shadethickets bound to the lake, watchful for travelers.

subzone:fargodeep-mine.text: Fargodeep Mine. Kobolds now swarm through Fargodeep Mine, south of Goldshire in central Elwynn Forest. Its gold once filled Stormwind's treasury, but now kobolds make their home in its tunnels. Gold once flowed from Fargodeep Mine into Stormwind's treasury. As the Kingdom's military presence in Elwynn dwindled, the outlying mine grew vulnerable. Kobolds filled its dark tunnels and made a warren beneath the hills. Now Marshal Dughan and Goldshire's authorities fear the lost ore and the danger to nearby farms, including the Stonefield and Maclure holdings. Fargodeep Mine runs through several levels, with lower shafts reaching deep beneath the forest floor. Kobold laborers and vermin hurry along wooden scaffolds, guarding the wax and gold dust they have scavenged. Goldtooth, a cunning kobold leader, lurks in a den above the main tunnels. He hoards trinkets stolen from travelers and nearby residents.

subzone:farstrider-lodge.text: Farstrider Lodge. In southeastern Loch Modan, Farstrider Lodge welcomes hunters and travelers bound for the wilds. Its high elven style sets it apart, though dwarves and humans live there too. Farstrider Lodge looks unlike the stone buildings of Khaz Modan. Its design recalls high elven craft, though Vyrin Swiftwind is the only known high elf still living there. Dwarves and humans make their homes beside him. No one knows who founded the lodge or when it was built. In the southeastern hills of Loch Modan, Farstrider Lodge offers hunters and travelers a place to stop before entering the wilds. Hunter and pet trainers work there, alongside merchants. Others come seeking help with local wildlife.

subzone:fel-rock.text: Fel Rock. North of Dolanaar, corruption spreads through Fel Rock and threatens Teldrassil’s woods. Lord Melenas and his grells have made the once-tranquil cavern a danger. North of Dolanaar, Fel Rock lies among Teldrassil’s wooded hills. Once peaceful, the cavern is now choked by twisted roots and strange shadows. Wild grells and grellkin roam within. The taint reaches into the boughs of the world tree. Lord Melenas, a satyr, has made Fel Rock his stronghold. From the cavern, he spreads corruption while night elf sentinels keep watch. Druids in Dolanaar, among them Tallonkai Swiftroot, seek defenders to cleanse the cave and slay Melenas. They must stop the blight before it reaches farther into the surrounding woods.

subzone:felfire-hill.text: Felfire Hill. In eastern Ashenvale, demons still crawl across the blighted rise of Felfire Hill. Infernals struck there during the Third War, and fel power still burns in the soil. Horde guards hold the bridges to the hill near their settlements. During the Third War, the Burning Legion sent flaming meteors across Kalimdor, carrying fearsome infernals. Several struck this ridge in Ashenvale. Their fires burned away the ancient woodland and corrupted the earth. The Legion fell at Mount Hyjal, yet demons that survived its defeat still prowl the scorched slopes. Fel energy saturates the land they haunt. Felfire Hill lies southeast of Splintertree Post and southwest of the Warsong Lumber Camp, near vital Horde operations. Demonic remnants threaten to spill into the surrounding forest. So Horde forces raised fortified barricades and guard towers at both bridges leading to the hill. The guards keep the creatures within their blighted haven.

subzone:fire-scar-shrine.text: Fire Scar Shrine. At Fire Scar Shrine, fel corruption has seized the old night elf place of worship southwest of Astranaar. Demons now gather among its altar stones. Southwest of Astranaar and west of the Ruins of Stardust, Fire Scar Shrine lies beneath a spreading blight. Servants of the Cult of the Dark Strand and the Shadow Council feed its corruption. Fel magic has scorched the earth, and demons gather openly among the trees. The forest's defenders face them there. Ilkrud Magthrull, an orc warlock, brought corruption to Fire Scar Shrine under Athrikus Narassin's orders. He served the Cult of the Dark Strand, alongside agents of the Shadow Council. Summoned fiends now patrol the altar stones unchecked. A tear in the veil sometimes draws greater horrors, including the towering doomguard Akkrilus.

subzone:forest-s-edge.text: Forest's Edge. At Forest's Edge, Riverpaw gnolls under Hogger threaten travelers on Elwynn's southwestern frontier. At Forest's Edge, the woods run southwest from Stormwind City, between Mirror Lake Orchard and the rivers that border Westfall. Westbrook Garrison is nearby, yet Stormwind has too few soldiers to keep the woods clear of wild beasts and raiding parties. Boars roam among the trees and along the banks. Riverpaw gnolls gather in force, using the woods as a staging ground. Hogger and his pack hunt through the woods of Forest's Edge. He is a massive, brutal gnoll chieftain who leads raids on nearby farms and harasses travelers. The Stormwind Army has placed a bounty on his head. His pack makes the timberland dangerous for anyone crossing it.

subzone:forest-song.text: Forest Song. In northeastern Ashenvale, Forest Song keeps watch near Satyrnaar and Bough Shadow. The ancient kaldorei ruins lie mostly deserted, with Kayneth Stillwind guarding the eastern border. Forest Song’s white columns and broken arches rise among the trees of northeastern Ashenvale. Once an elegant kaldorei settlement, the ruin now lies overgrown with ivy and wild ferns. Satyrnaar lies southwest, while the Warsong Lumber Camp presses in from the south. Eastern trails lead from here toward Azshara and Bough Shadow. Demonic corruption and Horde incursions trouble the woods, though the ruins remain quiet. Kayneth Stillwind keeps watch over Forest Song alone. From the crumbling outpost, the druid watches for enemies entering the wilderness, including the Forsaken in the eastern forests. Astranaar lies far away, and Forest Song has no garrison fortifications. Still, Alliance travelers bound north for Felwood or seeking the corruption spreading through the canopy can gather here.

subzone:forlorn-cavern.text: Forlorn Cavern. In Ironforge's northern depths, the Forlorn Cavern shelters those who keep to the shadows. Thieves, cutpurses, and practitioners of the dark arts conduct business there, far from the Great Forge and the dwarven guards. Cold and damp, the Forlorn Cavern lies beneath Ironforge's clang of anvils and the Great Forge's heat. Its winding paths follow the northern edge of the underground lake, hidden between the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Explorers. Rogues and warlocks train there, and vendors serve them. Weapon merchants and fishermen work beside the lake as well.

subzone:forlorn-rowe.text: Forlorn Rowe. At Raven Hill Cemetery's northern edge, Forlorn Rowe lies beneath a shadow of dread. Morbent Fel makes his home there, and his magic raises the restless dead across Duskwood. Forlorn Rowe climbs the northern edge of Raven Hill Cemetery in gloom. Morbent Fel makes his home on the hill. The necromancer raises many of the dead who roam the surrounding wilderness. From above, his foul enchantments command skeletal servants, making Duskwood's northwestern corner perilous for travelers.

subzone:freewind-post.text:
Freewind Post. Freewind Post guards the Horde’s hold in Thousand Needles from a high canyon mesa. Tauren lifts and winding rope bridges lead to its refuge, where the Horde faces centaur warbands and prepares for the frontier. Freewind Post clings to the canyon mesas, where height helps guard its people. Galak centaur command the arid floor, but cannot climb the sheer cliffs or easily breach the heavy wooden lifts that carry Horde travelers upward. Rope and plank bridges link the post to neighboring spires, sheltering the outpost above.

Harpies screech along the bluffs, while the tauren tend the nearby wyvern grounds at Highperch. There, they cull wild eggs and raise the hatchlings as loyal wind rider mounts for the Horde.

subzone:frostmane-hold.text: Frostmane Hold. Frostmane trolls raid from the cliffs south of Gnomeregan in western Dun Morogh. The Ironforge Guard watches their camp and caverns as the raiders press into dwarven lands. In western Dun Morogh, Frostmane Hold cuts into cold cliffs. Rough structures stand outside its winding caves, where hideskinners and headhunters guard the tribe’s stronghold. From here, Frostmane raiders strike the valleys, threaten travelers on mountain passes, and test the defenses around Kharanos. Dwarven commanders in Kharanos fear the growing Frostmane force. Young mountaineers and adventurers scout the caverns and map their defenses. They thin the warbands before the tribe can gather for an organized assault on dwarven outposts.

subzone:frostmane-hovel.text: Frostmane Hovel. In southern Coldridge Valley, Frostmane trolls press toward the dwarven training grounds. Frostmane trolls shelter in caverns cut into the mountains south of Coldridge Valley. They refuse to yield the high snows to Ironforge and raid nearby dwarven camps. Their attacks disrupt the supply lines into the valley.

subzone:furlbrow-s-pumpkin-farm.text: Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm. Bandits and harvest golems hold Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm in northern Westfall, off the road from Elwynn Forest. Farmer Furlbrow and Verna have lost their home to the Defias Brotherhood. Near Westfall's northern border, Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm once fed the kingdom. The Defias Brotherhood drove Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna from their land. Now mechanical harvest golems roam the fields and attack anyone who approaches. Bandits occupy the farm buildings, while the rightful owners camp beside the road near the Jansen Stead, mourning their home and livelihood. The Defias Brotherhood has claimed homesteads like Furlbrow's while Stormwind's military garrison struggles to protect Westfall's rural farmers. Bandits camp at the farm and use it as a staging ground. Lethal harvest watchers guard the perimeter, leaving travelers on the nearby highway open to ambush.

subzone:galardell-valley.text: Galardell Valley. Gnolls prowl Galardell Valley beneath the Tower of Ilgalar in northeastern Redridge. The valley threatens the nearby settlements. Redridge gnolls prowl Galardell Valley, beyond the reach of Lakeshire's defenders. They roam the lowlands and camp along the canyon floor, under brutal pack leaders such as Lieutenant Fangore. Above the ravines rises the Tower of Ilgalar, stronghold of the renegade mage Morganth. Together, gnolls and tower make the valley a source of dread for nearby settlements.

subzone:gates-of-ironforge.text: Gates of Ironforge. From Dun Morogh, travelers climb to the Gates of Ironforge, where a stone king guards the way into the dwarven capital. The gates open in the mountain face, with High King Modimus Anvilmar's statue just inside. From central Dun Morogh, you climb a winding, fortified ramp through the snowy lowlands to the Gates of Ironforge. Beyond the great portal stands a stone likeness of High King Modimus Anvilmar. He united the dwarven clans before the War of the Three Hammers. The passage opens into the Commons, where Ironforge's trade and banking are centered.

subzone:goblin-foundry.text: Goblin Foundry. In the Deadmines, goblins keep the Goblin Foundry working for the Defias Brotherhood. Gilnid oversees the craftsmen and engineers around its great smelting cauldron. Deep beneath Moonbrook, goblin craftsmen and engineers labor for the Defias Brotherhood. Smelters and iron ramps fill the chamber. There, they make anchors and cannonballs. Gilnid, the smelter, oversees the goblin workforce. Craftsmen keep production moving while engineers send remote-controlled golems to defend the workshop. Narrow ramps and molten metal make the chamber dangerous for intruders.

subzone:gol-bolar-quarry.text:
Gol'Bolar Quarry. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, troggs have driven the miners from the snowy hills of southeastern Dun Morogh. The Ironforge dwarves came for stone and ore, but now the dig lies quiet. Ironforge dwarves opened Gol'Bolar Quarry southeast of Kharanos to draw stone and mineral wealth from the mountains. Their digging broke into underground warrens and brought a horde of hostile troggs into the open. The creatures soon drove out the miners.

The upper camp is now an embattled staging ground. Overseers, tradesfolk, and Prospector Gehn gather dwarven and gnomish recruits there to drive the troggs back and reclaim the pit.

subzone:gol-bolar-quarry-mine.text: Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine. Troggs hold Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine beneath the quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. Dwarves of Ironforge mined its tunnels for stone and rich ore until their picks broke into trogg caverns. Now Hammerspine leads the warband in the deepest shafts. The dwarves' pickaxes broke through a wall into caverns where troggs dwelled. Their mining ended there. Troggs poured from the darkness, overwhelmed the crews, and drove them from the mine. The abandoned shafts remain in trogg hands. Younger troggs roam the quarry's sunlit terraces, but the mine shelters the warband's fiercest fighters. Deep in its cramped tunnels lurks Hammerspine, their vicious chieftain. Local mountaineers still need to reclaim the valuable quarry. To do so, they must reach the mine's deepest shafts and cut off the troggs at their source.

subzone:gold-coast-quarry.text: Gold Coast Quarry. In southwestern Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood holds Gold Coast Quarry and draws on its remaining riches for rebellion. Once, its stone, minerals, and gold helped rebuild Stormwind. Stormwind once drew stone and gold from Gold Coast Quarry to rebuild the kingdom. After royal troops left Westfall, Defias highwaymen and renegade laborers seized the mine. Now Brotherhood patrols watch from its terraced ramps above the coast and take the minerals still left there to fund their rebellion.

subzone:goldshire.text: Goldshire. Goldshire stands where Elwynn’s roads meet, between Stormwind City, Westfall, Redridge, and the southern frontier. Rebuilt after the First War, it offers travelers the Lion’s Pride Inn, while a hard-pressed Stormwind Guard defends the town. Goldshire holds the crossroads in rural Elwynn, where the king’s highways meet. Threats press closer as Stormwind’s forces thin and King Varian Wrynn remains mysteriously absent. Marshal Dughan must rely on passing adventurers instead of regular troops to guard the borders. Riverpaw gnolls push in from the west, while hostile murlocs claim the shores of Stone Cairn Lake and Crystal Lake. Their attacks have killed royal guards and brought danger close to town. Goldshire and Moonbrook were the last strongholds to fall in the First War. Warchief Blackhand cut King Llane Wrynn I off from his realm before sacking Stormwind Keep, and the Orcish Horde overwhelmed both towns. Goldshire was reduced to ash and lay barren until it was rebuilt after the Second War.

subzone:grand-vestibule.text: Grand Vestibule. At the Grand Vestibule, Scarlet sentries guard the passage into the monastery’s inner halls. Crimson pillars and statues of fallen crusaders line the entrance. Past the Scarlet Monastery’s outer gates, you enter a marble hall lined with pillars and statues of armored champions. Scarlet sentries, disciples, and augurs patrol the flagstones. They strike down anyone who enters without the order’s crimson tabard. Here, the Crusade’s strict discipline meets its fervor. Every intruder must cross the Grand Vestibule to reach the monastery’s guarded inner wings. Alliance champions sent north and Horde forces advancing from the nearby Undercity both face the Crusade’s defenders beneath its high arches. Beyond them lie the inner cloisters.

subzone:great-forge.text:
Great Forge. At Ironforge’s center, the Great Forge keeps its fires burning and smiths at work. Its Great Anvil draws people from across the mountain city. The Great Forge was the first structure the early dwarves built beneath Ironforge Mountain. The capital grew outward in rings around it. Molten stone and slag run from giant foundries through glowing channels, lighting the cavern with an amber haze.

At the center, Master of the Forge Myolor Sunderfury oversees the massive Great Anvil. Masters of metalwork gather around its rim to hammer armor, tools, and weapons day and night. Smithing is only part of the Great Forge’s work. Guild offices, supply shops, and the city’s main gryphon roost ring the chamber. Gryth Thurden tends the roost, where travelers from across the Alliance mingle amid the hammer blows.

subzone:great-lift.text: Great Lift. At the Great Lift, travelers cross between the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles. Tauren platforms carry people and supplies between the rim and canyon floor, while quilboar threaten the southern road. At the rim between the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles, two wooden platforms hang over the canyon. Heavy timber, braided rope, and counterweighted pulleys carry caravans, couriers, and warriors across the sheer drop. Brave Moonhorn watches from the top platform, and Grish Longrunner keeps watch below. They guide travelers along the road and help cargo pass safely. The road to the Great Lift crosses hostile ground in the southern Barrens. Quilboar tribes have pushed south and now threaten the route between Thousand Needles and the northern trails. Travelers making the long journey must fend off razorfen raiders before they reach the wooden platforms.

subzone:greatwood-vale.text: Greatwood Vale. In eastern Stonetalon, the Grimtotem hold Greatwood Vale and strike at nearby settlements. The dangerous Webwinder Path leads into the forested valley, now their base for bloody assaults. Greatwood Vale has become a violent frontier off the Webwinder Path. Grundig Darkcloud leads the Grimtotem who have moved into the vale in force. They bar safe passage and terrorize the surrounding foothills. From Greatwood Vale, Grimtotem raiders swept into nearby Camp Aparaje and slaughtered nearly every tauren there. Makaba Flathoof escaped.
