subzone:shadowthread-cave.text: Shadowthread Cave. In Shadowthread Cave, spiders now threaten the young kaldorei near Aldrassil. The cave lies beneath Shadowglen’s northwest cliffs. In Shadowglen’s shaded northwest, Shadowthread Cave shelters Teldrassil’s giant spiders. Once they lived quietly among the World Tree’s young boughs. Now the brood guards its territory fiercely. Webwood silk chokes the stone corridors, and the spiders threaten young kaldorei who venture beyond Aldrassil. Githyiss the Vile rules Shadowthread Cave’s deepest recesses. The monstrous broodmother is far more ferocious than the common webwood crawlers. Young night elf sentinels and druids enter the cave to curb the infestation and slay her. Corruption touches Teldrassil’s wildlife, and the sanctuary of Shadowglen is at risk.

subzone:shimmer-ridge.text: Shimmer Ridge. In northern Dun Morogh, Shimmer Ridge lies west of the Gates of Ironforge, where Frostmane trolls hold two camps across a chasm. Shimmerweed grows nowhere else. Frostmane trolls hold camps on both sides of a chasm, joined by a rickety wooden bridge. Troll scavengers and tamed mountain boars guard the rocky heights. The ridge lies near the main road and the dwarven capital, giving the trolls a place to raid travelers and mountain patrols. Frostmane trolls grow shimmerweed on the ridge. Dwarven brewmasters prize the plant for the potent, flavorful highland ales it makes. Since it is hard to gather elsewhere, mountaineers and young recruits brave troll ambushes and tusked beasts to harvest it from the trolls' plots.

subzone:shimmering-flats.text: Shimmering Flats. At Thousand Needles' southeastern edge, the Shimmering Flats stretch between the salt pan and Tanaris. The old lakebed now draws racers to the Mirage Raceway, where gnome and goblin tinkerers test their machines among desert beasts. Beneath the southern sun, the Shimmering Flats lie bare, with bleached turtle bones and the wooden wreck of an ancient sailing vessel. Their level salt crust makes them Kalimdor's chief ground for testing experimental vehicles. At the heart of the flats, the Mirage Raceway gathers gnome and goblin tinkerers for fierce contests. Rocket cars, gyrocopters and engines roar across the salt. Their makers chase speed, and fiery crashes leave smoking craters behind. Beyond the raceway, hardened basilisks, aggressive scorpids and circling vultures hunt across the open flats. Farther south, the ground turns treacherous around the Rustmaul Dig Site. Dwarven prospectors first excavated the quarry, then the Horde contested it. The site was abandoned when picks broke into underground tunnels and unleashed vicious silithid across the southern edge of the flats.

subzone:shrine-of-aessina.text: Shrine of Aessina. At the Shrine of Aessina, night elves honor an ancient spirit of nature and wild creatures. The shrine lies in southwestern Ashenvale, between Maestra's Post and Astranaar, where border friction is growing. West of Astranaar, night elves honor Aessina, a Wild God who bears the heart and spirit of the deep forests. For generations, they and their woodland kin have come here to commune with nature, far from the main roads. The Horde presses into Ashenvale for timber and footholds, and peace grows uncertain at sacred grounds across the territory.

subzone:si-7-stormwind-city.text:
SI:7 (Stormwind City). In Old Town, SI:7 watches for threats to Stormwind from a fortified stone manor. Master Mathias Shaw directs the kingdom’s intelligence service from behind its heavy doors. In Old Town, SI:7 works from a fortified stone manor. From the street, it could pass for an ordinary home or military barracks. Master Mathias Shaw directs Stormwind Intelligence, Section 7. Its agents gather intelligence, watch suspected threats and carry out secret operations to guard the kingdom from subversion.

The city guard patrols Stormwind’s streets, while the Royal Guard protects Stormwind Keep. SI:7 trains handlers and sends covert agents against foreign enemies, saboteurs and unrest within the kingdom.

subzone:silver-stream-mine.text: Silver Stream Mine. In northern Loch Modan, Silver Stream Mine lies between Algaz Station and the Stonewrought Dam. Its silver veins are spent, and Tunnel Rat kobolds now hoard stolen equipment and rare minerals in the Miners' League depot. Silver Stream Mine once sent rich silver to Ironforge. Dwarf miners worked its veins until they ran dry, leaving broad chambers beneath the earth. The Miners' League put those hard-won shafts to use as a guarded storehouse for tools, mining crates, and regional equipment. The mine also yields Charged Rift Gems, which draw arcanists seeking delicate tailoring reagents. Tunnel Rat kobolds came in great numbers and drove the Miners' League caretakers out into the cold of Loch Modan. Now they guard the stolen dwarf crates with manic fervor. Beyond the rear entrances, shattered orcish catapults and wagons lie forgotten, remnants of older frontier skirmishes.

subzone:silverwind-refuge.text: Silverwind Refuge. Sentinels guard Silverwind Refuge in south-central Ashenvale, just north of Mystral Lake. Travelers find shelter along the forest trails. Silverwind Refuge lies between Mystral Lake and Iris Lake, with Iris Lake to the north. Alongside Astranaar, it is one of central Ashenvale’s chief night elven waystations. Craftsmen and wilderness trainers teach herbalism, alchemy, skinning, and hunting. Sentinels guard the refuge, where allies crossing the ancient woods can rest.

subzone:silverwing-grove.text: Silverwing Grove. Silverwing Sentinels muster at Silverwing Grove in south-central Ashenvale, near Fallen Sky Lake. From this fortified hollow, night elf warriors gather Alliance forces against the Warsong Clan loggers cutting through the forest. Beneath the canopy southwest of Silverwing Outpost, Silverwing Sentinels gather at Silverwing Grove. They use the post to oppose the Horde's lumbering in Warsong Gulch. Alliance officers, provisions, and scouts assemble here to organize skirmishes and muster champions. Together, they defend Ashenvale against orcish expansion.

subzone:silverwing-outpost.text: Silverwing Outpost. At Silverwing Outpost, Duriel Moonfire commands the Alliance’s easternmost hold against the Horde in contested Ashenvale. The garrison guards the eastern bank of the Falfarren River in the forest’s south-central reaches. Southwest of Splintertree Post and just north of the Barrens border, Silverwing Outpost holds the eastern bank of the Falfarren River. The Horde contests and patrols this ground. From here, the garrison shields night elf holdings deeper in the forest. Duriel Moonfire and her Silverwing Sentinels face constant attacks from nearby orcs seeking to drive night elf forces away.

subzone:sishir-canyon.text: Sishir Canyon. Webs and Deepmoss spiders choke Sishir Canyon, the eastern pass through the Stonetalon Mountains. Travelers face the brood on the dangerous way to the Ruins of Eldre'thar. Sishir Canyon cuts through the Stonetalon Mountains toward the ancient Ruins of Eldre'thar. Deepmoss spiders have overrun the gorge. Sheets of web cover its stone floor and walls, and egg sacs cluster among them. Travelers and sentinels heading for the night elven ruins must fight through swarms of aggressive webspinners. Deep in Sishir Canyon, Besseleth rules as matriarch of the Deepmoss brood. Her great size and venom threaten anyone trying to secure the pass. Local forces in Stonetalon keep watch and warn travelers that scattered spiders are not all that lurks in the webbed depths. Besseleth fiercely guards her brood.

subzone:slaughtered-lamb.text: Slaughtered Lamb. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, the Slaughtered Lamb keeps a quiet, seedy tavern above a hidden warlock sanctuary. Dark corners and few patrons greet you at the Slaughtered Lamb, where barkeep Jarel Moor warns visitors to avoid the shadows. The warning is literal. Back passages descend to crypts and summoning circles below. There, human warlocks and transfer practitioners from Khaz Modan study fel arcana, beyond the disapproving eyes of the Church of the Holy Light and the Kirin Tor.

subzone:south-gate-outpost.text: South Gate Outpost. At South Gate Outpost, mountaineers guard the pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Their fortified post watches the southern road from Ironforge's frigid heights to the Loch's temperate valley. At South Gate Outpost, snowy slopes give way to Loch Modan's basin. Ironforge mountaineers patrol the rocky switchbacks and keep dangerous wildlife off the main highway. Their kin at North Gate Outpost face a harder fight, but the southern road is largely secure. Travelers, pilgrims, and trade wagons can reach Thelsamar in relative safety.

subzone:south-gate-pass.text: South Gate Pass. Travelers cross South Gate Pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Its guarded road links Ironforge with Thelsamar. South Gate Pass cuts through the Khaz Modan range, joining Dun Morogh's high mountains to Loch Modan's valley in the east. Stone archways mark the way from cold slopes into warmer dwarven heartlands. The road leads toward Thelsamar, carrying mountaineers, couriers, and newly trained adventurers setting out from the capital. Dwarven mountaineers keep watch at South Gate Outpost, guarding the pass against wild beasts and prowling troggs. The road is safer than the untamed parts of the valley, though hostile wildlife and roving threats still test its approaches. Stay on the road as you travel.

subzone:southshore.text:
Southshore. In Hillsbrad, Southshore shelters the Alliance amid the ruins of Lordaeron. Once a quiet fishing village, the coastal port now faces the Forsaken at Tarren Mill, Syndicate bandits, and monsters along the shore. Refugee boats from the fallen kingdom of Stormwind first brought Southshore to prominence during the First War. The town was contested and overrun during the Second War, then rebuilt. It endured the horrors of the Third War as well.

Now much of Lordaeron lies in ruins or under Forsaken rule, but Southshore remains loyal to the Grand Alliance. It shelters displaced human survivors, veteran paladins of the Silver Hand, and scholars of the Kirin Tor. Southshore's docks see the ship between Menethil Harbor and Auberdine, and the town is known for its turtle bisque. Yet life here is perilous. Magistrate Henry Maleb and Marshal Redpath lead the town as it faces pressure from every side.

To the north, the Forsaken of Tarren Mill fight a bitter border conflict for control of Hillsbrad. Inland, Syndicate outlaws raid supply lines and assassinate local leaders. Ogres, murlocs, and naga also harass the town's borders.

subzone:splintertree-post.text: Splintertree Post. In eastern Ashenvale, Splintertree Post holds the Horde’s frontier northwest of Felfire Hill. Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan raised it during the Third War as a fortified base against the night elves and a staging ground for expansion. Splintertree Post anchors the Horde’s military and supply lines across eastern Ashenvale. Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan founded it when the orcs first entered the forest during the Third War. Orcish and tauren scouts and warriors still guard the armed outpost. An inn, a flight master, and steady supplies from Orgrimmar support the Horde’s contested hold beneath the trees. Splintertree Post stays ready for attack. The night elves have neither forgotten nor forgiven Grommash’s actions during the war. They also oppose the Horde’s continued logging and its raids on Astranaar. Sentinels hide in the surrounding woods and strike in constant retaliation, testing the post’s watchmen at all hours.

subzone:splithoof-crag.text: Splithoof Crag. Galak centaur patrol the northern cliffs of Splithoof Crag and guard their canyon stronghold. Their settlement surrounds Splithoof Hold, while they contest the ravine below the Grimtotem heights. On the northern rock face of Thousand Needles, east of Darkcloud Pinnacle, Galak centaur keep their stronghold. Crude tents and dirt paths fill the enclave. Against the cliff stands Splithoof Hold, a cavern beneath the settlement. There, the Galak guard the Cloven Hoof, an ancient centaur relic kept beside a sacred brazier. Galak centaur attack travelers, Horde expeditions, and tauren scouts passing beneath their bluffs. The Grimtotem occupy nearby high pinnacles. Yet the Galak hold the canyon ravine and the caverns beneath its stone.

subzone:splithoof-hold.text: Splithoof Hold. Galak centaur guard Splithoof Hold in the caves of Splithoof Crag. Within, the Ancient Brazier keeps their sacred flame burning without end. Within Splithoof Crag, Galak centaur defend their cavern against rival tribes and travelers crossing Thousand Needles. Its deep shelter protects them from the windswept canyon floor. Chokepoints guard the way in, with a secure refuge inside the rock. Deep within Splithoof Hold, the Ancient Brazier cradles the Sacred Flame. The mystic fire burns without end. The centaur honor it in ritual, while spiritual wanderers from across the canyon come to wonder at its power.

subzone:starbreeze-village.text: Starbreeze Village. Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Starbreeze Village, east of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. The once quiet night elf hamlet lies in ruins beneath the corruption spreading through the World Tree. Southeast of Shadowglen, just down the road from Dolanaar, Starbreeze Village lies in shambles. Night elf families once lived peacefully beneath Teldrassil’s boughs. Now aggressive Gnarlpine furbolgs occupy the wooden homes. Corruption afflicting the World Tree’s boughs has driven them wild. They drove out the elven residents and fiercely defend the ruined grounds.

subzone:steelgrill-s-depot.text: Steelgrill's Depot. East of Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot keeps Alliance vehicles and machinery working. Beldin Steelgrill and his crew repair them, supply tinkerers, and salvage what they can. Just off the snowy road, dwarven miners and eccentric gnome engineers gather among heavy machinery, mechanized walking frames, and raw ore from nearby quarries. Metal clanks, steam vents hiss, and experimental engines churn. Trogg disruptions and shortages of mechanical supplies trouble Dun Morogh. In the bitter cold, travelers come for spare parts or technical guidance.

subzone:stendel-s-pond.text: Stendel's Pond. At Stendel's Pond, anglers still come for fresh fish despite the gnolls along its banks. Southwest of Sentinel Hill, Stendel's Pond still draws anglers. Gnolls roam the muddy banks, where scattered skeletons and two lone graves mark a perilous shore. No one knows whether foul water or the beasts caused the deaths. Yet schools of sagefish still bring anglers to the pond.

subzone:stone-cairn-lake.text: Stone Cairn Lake. At Stone Cairn Lake in northeastern Elwynn, murlocs hold the southern shore. Renegade wizards camp beside Heroes' Vigil, a memorial to those lost in the First War. Families and pilgrims once crossed the calm lake waters to honor the dead at Heroes' Vigil. The stone memorial rises on the central island, marking the heavy loss of human life in the First War against the Orcish Horde. Now the island is hostile, and those who come to pay their respects must face the wizards' camp beside the monument. Aggressive murlocs hold Stone Cairn Lake's southern banks. Crude huts line the water, and the murlocs harass anyone who comes near. Rich mineral veins run through the hills and rocky outcrops around the lake, drawing prospectors and miners despite the dangers along the shore.

subzone:stonefield-farm.text: Stonefield Farm. In southern Elwynn Forest, the Stonefield family works its fields while a long feud divides them from the Maclures. South of Goldshire, the Stonefields grow crops for the realm. For decades, they have quarreled with the nearby Maclure Vineyards. Each household accuses the other of theft and trespassing, and even small disputes keep tensions high. Gramma Stonefield, Ma Stonefield, and young Tommy Joe Stonefield make their home here.

subzone:stonefire-tavern.text:
Stonefire Tavern. In Ironforge’s Commons, travelers find the Stonefire Tavern just north of the city gates. Its hearth, dwarven ale, and rooms offer rest to those arriving from across Khaz Modan. In Ironforge’s Commons, just north of the fortress gates, Innkeeper Firebrew runs Stonefire Tavern with his daughter Gwenna. Weary wayfarers can find meals, local brews, and lodging beneath the mountain.

Travelers come from across the Alliance to rest from Dun Morogh’s mountain snows, trade tales, or gather supplies before exploring the city. The hearth draws them together at the heart of the Commons.

subzone:stonesplinter-valley.text:
Stonesplinter Valley. In southwestern Loch Modan, Stonesplinter troggs hold a mountain vale behind crude defenses. Their chieftain, Grawmug, leads the tribe from within. Among the crags of southwestern Loch Modan, Stonesplinter troggs have made their stronghold. Troggs clawed up from underground across Khaz Modan and ended the quiet that once filled this hollow. The Stonesplinter tribe claimed the valley and carved crude defenses into its rocky passes.

They dug dens and raised barricades, and now hunt anything that comes too close. Their numbers threaten the roads through southern Loch Modan. So Mountaineers from Thelsamar hire mercenaries to thin the tribe and bring down Grawmug, its towering warlord.

subzone:stonetalon-peak.text: Stonetalon Peak. At Stonetalon Peak, kaldorei Sentinels and druids guard an ancient sanctuary. Its sheltered valley is sacred to the night elves and remains the Alliance’s main foothold in the high mountains. High above the dry lower ranges, Stonetalon Peak opens into a green valley. Its ruins reach back millennia to temples that honored Queen Azshara before the Great Sundering. Night elven Sentinels and druids care for the sanctuary now. They keep a barrow den and an Alliance flight roost here. During the Third War, Jaina Proudmoore’s human expedition and Thrall’s Horde climbed Stonetalon Peak, each seeking the Oracle in the deep caverns. Medivh’s visions had led them there. When they met, these mortal enemies laid down their blades. Their uneasy pact helped them stand against the Burning Legion at Mount Hyjal. Sentinel patrols still guard the peak, and Horde incursions in the lowlands keep its defenders alert.

subzone:stonewatch.text:
Stonewatch. Blackrock orcs hold Stonewatch above the approaches from the Burning Steppes, and Lakeshire faces their threat. The fortress once guarded Redridge against invasions from the north. Stonewatch overlooks the cliffs near Stonewatch Falls. Its tower and keep command the approaches from the Burning Steppes. Lakeshire's defenders held the fortress first, until Morganth, a rogue warlock, allied with the Blackrock clan. With dark magic, the orcs overwhelmed the 12th Sabre Regiment and seized the keep.

Morganth then turned against his allies and withdrew to the nearby Tower of Ilgalar with an army of Shadowhide gnolls. The Blackrock orcs held Stonewatch under Warlord Gath'Ilzogg and Lieutenant Tharil'zun. Blackrock orcs hold Stonewatch, leaving Lakeshire open to conquest. Stormwind's House of Nobles has sent no substantial military reinforcements, whether from indifference or paralysis. Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris have had to hire mercenaries and call for volunteers.

Their best hope of lifting the threat over the region is to strike at the fortress's leaders, Tharil'zun and Gath'Ilzogg.

subzone:stonewatch-falls.text: Stonewatch Falls. Water spills into a murloc-claimed pool at Stonewatch Falls, beneath Stonewatch in the eastern Redridge Mountains. Stonewatch Falls pours down the slope beneath Stonewatch, the Blackrock orc stronghold. Its water runs from Lake Everstill’s eastern river and gathers in a deep pool against the mountainside. Murlocs have claimed the shore with crude reed hovels, and prey on travelers who come too close to the water.

subzone:stonewatch-keep.text:
Stonewatch Keep. Blackrock orcs now hold Stonewatch Keep in eastern Redridge Mountains and turn its walls against Lakeshire. The Kingdom of Stormwind built and manned the fortress before the invaders seized it as a base for their warlords. Stonewatch Keep once guarded the eastern ridges and Lakeshire's settlers from hostile incursions. Then the renegade warlock Morganth joined forces with the Blackrock clan. His dark magic strengthened the orcs, who stormed the fortress and overcame its human defenders. After the victory, Morganth abandoned the clan to raise the nearby Tower of Ilgalar and subjugate local gnolls. The Blackrock orcs kept the keep as a staging ground for attacks on the valley. A strong Blackrock garrison holds Stonewatch Keep under the orc warlord Gath'Ilzogg and his lieutenant, Tharil'zun. From the ramparts, they direct raids across Redridge and take prisoners, among them Stormwind's Corporal Keeshan.

Stormwind's forces are spread thin, so the kingdom cannot send a full regiment to reclaim the fortress. Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris have hired mercenary champions to enter the stronghold and kill the Blackrock leaders before Lakeshire is overrun.

subzone:stonewatch-tower.text:
Stonewatch Tower. Blackrock sentinels hold Stonewatch Tower in northeastern Redridge. Once Lakeshire's outpost, it now helps the clan watch the ridges and guard its mountain stronghold. Above Lake Everstill, Stonewatch Tower guards the high mountain passes. The Kingdom of Stormwind built it as a forward scout for Stonewatch Keep. From its heights, sentries watched the eastern ridges and warned Lakeshire of threats from the Burning Steppes.

Then Warlord Gath'Ilzogg's Blackrock orcs swept down from the heights. They overcame the human defenders and seized the stronghold for their war effort. Blackrock sentinels now watch the tower, keeping Alliance scouts from reaching the fortress unseen.

subzone:stonewrought-dam.text: Stonewrought Dam. Along Loch Modan’s northern rim, waters gather behind Stonewrought Dam. The dwarven barrier holds back the Loch and drains the Wetlands below into habitable marshes. East of Dun Algaz, Stonewrought Dam spans a canyon in one of the great works of dwarven craft. Dark Iron architect Franclorn Forgewright designed it and pioneered the stonewrought technique used to raise it. By holding water in the mountain basin, the dam doubled the Loch’s surface area and steadily lowered the waters to the north. The Wetlands formed from a valley once wholly flooded. Stonewrought Dam now serves Ironforge, but Dark Iron saboteurs from the southern mountains target it. After recent assaults and attempts to slip inside, Ironforge placed a garrison here under Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh. Guards and engineers patrol the masonry day and night. Should the dam be breached, the Loch could drain and send a devastating flood across the Wetlands below.

subzone:stormwind-gate.text: Stormwind Gate. Stormwind Gate stands open between Elwynn Forest and Stormwind City, watched by sentries. Beyond its arch, stone monuments line the Valley of Heroes. The Stormwind City Guard holds this passage, and patrols march from the outer arch toward the Valley of Heroes. Unrest lingers in Elwynn, yet the iron and stone gates remain open. Travelers, merchants, and defenders returning from the road pass through toward the heart of the Alliance.

subzone:stormwind-keep.text: Stormwind Keep. Stormwind Keep holds the royal court above the capital. Rebuilt after its ruin in the First War, it is now home to the young boy-king Anduin Wrynn and his regent, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Stormwind Keep crowns a plateau above the city, with halls for the crown and the kingdom’s defense. The Old Horde burned the first stronghold after King Llane was assassinated near the end of the First War. After the Alliance reclaimed the kingdom, builders raised the keep again on its old foundations. Its halls include the grand throne room and the War Room, while garden courtyards and the Royal Library offer quieter spaces.

subzone:stormwind-stockade.text: Stormwind Stockade. Stormwind Stockade has fallen into chaos beneath the canals near the Mage Quarter. A coordinated revolt has driven the guards from the lower cells, and the prison's most dangerous prisoners roam free. Warden Thelwater oversees the Stockade, where Stormwind holds cutthroats, Defias operatives, captured Blackrock orcs, and Dark Iron dwarves. The Defias conspirator Bazil Thredd led the uprising, and now prisoners roam the corridors. Thelwater has secured the entrance, but the revolt still threatens to spill into the canals. He needs adventurers to enter the prison and put it down.

subzone:stormwind-stockade-classic.text: Stormwind Stockade (Classic). A revolt has put the prisoners in control beneath Stormwind City's canal district. The Stockade lies beside the canals between Old Town and the Mage Quarter. Warden Thelwater oversees the Stockade, where Stormwind holds its most dangerous prisoners. Among them are Defias Brotherhood cutthroats, a Blackrock orc, an ogre and a Dark Iron dwarf. Then Bazil Thredd led a coordinated riot that overwhelmed the garrison. The surviving guards fled, and prisoners now rule the halls.

subzone:stoutlager-inn.text: Stoutlager Inn. In Thelsamar, Stoutlager Inn welcomes travelers crossing western Loch Modan with a warm hearth and a place to gather. Stoutlager Inn draws miners, mountaineers, and travelers passing between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands. They trade rumors, find beds, and share dwarven ale beneath its roof. Beyond Thelsamar, troggs and kobolds make the wilderness dangerous, so the inn’s stone walls and fires offer welcome shelter.

subzone:strahnbrad.text: Strahnbrad. Syndicate brigands hold Strahnbrad, a ruined town in the northeastern heights of the Alterac Mountains. Near the Western Plaguelands border, it has fallen into decay since Prince Arthas Menethil defended it from Blackrock orc raiders. Strahnbrad belonged to the Kingdom of Alterac until Lordaeron absorbed it after the Second War. On the eve of the Third War, Blackrock clan orcs raided the town to take human sacrifices for the Burning Legion. Prince Arthas Menethil rode to its defense with the Knights of the Silver Hand. He drove off the raiders and slew their slave master, but Strahnbrad was left bloodied. Soon after, the Scourge brought down Lordaeron, and the town was abandoned to the elements. The Syndicate uses Strahnbrad as an operations hub. Displaced Alteraci nobles and outlaws patrol the abandoned town hall and blacksmith, now their hideouts and staging grounds as they plan to reclaim their fallen realm. The Syndicate keeps supplies and captive labor in the ruins, including the orc Gol'dir. Horde scouts from Tarren Mill seek to free him.

subzone:sun-rock-retreat.text: Sun Rock Retreat. In the high basin south of Mirkfallon Lake, Sun Rock Retreat shelters the Horde among Stonetalon's peaks. The tauren hold this ground sacred, and orcs and tauren use the settlement as a base and supply post. South of Mirkfallon Lake, Sun Rock Retreat rests in a mountain basin the tauren have long held sacred. Their ancient tradition says An'she, the Sun, kissed the peak above the village. Before the Horde came, tauren shamans and pilgrims traveled here for rites that crossed the mortal veil. They drew strength from the land's close bond with the spirit world. Orcs and tauren now hold Sun Rock Retreat as the Horde's chief base across the Stonetalon Mountains. Together they seek a secure foothold against hostile harpy broods, local night elf sentinels, and the Venture Company's industrial pillaging. Trade and flight routes link the retreat with Thunder Bluff, the Crossroads, and the borders of Ashenvale. Here, those who brave the crags find shelter, provisions, and spiritual guidance.

subzone:talondeep-path.text:
Talondeep Path. Beneath the ridge, Talondeep Path links Ashenvale with the Stonetalon Mountains. Its quiet tunnel runs from the woods west of Mystral Lake to Windshear Crag. Talondeep Path runs beneath the ridge between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. It joins the woods west of Mystral Lake to the northwestern reaches of Windshear Crag. Surface trails cross dangerous country, where predators and warring factions roam. The tunnel stays calm, with no hostile beasts or encampments.

Side pockets twist away from the passage, and crevices and natural alcoves break up the rock. Above ground, faint traces of an old road remain along the peaks. Travelers once crossed there before taking the route through the stone.

subzone:talondeep-vale.text: Talondeep Vale. In south-central Ashenvale, the wooded vale carries travelers toward the Stonetalon Mountains. Talondeep Vale lies beneath Ashenvale’s trees. Silverwind Refuge stands to the east, with the Ruins of Stardust nearby. To the south, the land rises toward the Stonetalon Mountains. Travelers cross the valley between Ashenvale’s heart and the high crags beyond.

subzone:tarren-mill.text:
Tarren Mill. In northern Hillsbrad Foothills, Tarren Mill holds the Horde's line beneath the Alterac Mountains. Once a peaceful human farming village, it is now a Forsaken outpost locked in conflict with Southshore to the south. Since the Third War, Tarren Mill's fields and mill have fallen silent. Before then, the town thrived on farming and served Lordaeron. During the Second War, Alliance forces near Tarren Mill freed high elven archers from orc encampments. Their rescue secured Quel'Thalas's full commitment to the Alliance of Lordaeron.

The town's living inhabitants are gone, replaced by the Forsaken. Its buildings are weathered, its fields barren, and its mill quiet. The Forsaken fortify Tarren Mill against mountain beasts, Syndicate outlaws, and Alliance skirmishers. Tarren Mill is the Horde's forward base in Hillsbrad. Southshore, the Alliance port, lies directly across from it, and the road between the towns has become a warzone. From Tarren Mill, Horde travelers push back against the human farmers and soldiers occupying Hillsbrad. They also coordinate strikes against dwarven excavators at Dun Garok and secure the dangerous roads that climb into the snowy crags of the Alterac Mountains.

subzone:temple-gardens.text: Temple Gardens. In Temple Gardens, water and bridges gather at the heart of Darnassus. The city bank stands on the main island, beside the Temple of the Moon to the south and a glowing tree portal to Teldrassil's base. Water runs beneath wooden bridges through Darnassus's center. They link the Temple Gardens' islets with the Cenarion Enclave to the north, the terraces to the east, and the Temple of the Moon to the south. Night elves tend the waters and foliage. Travelers and priestesses find a quiet place to rest. Darnassus's central vault and bank occupy the main island. On its western bank, a great glowing pink tree portal carries travelers through the boughs to Rut'theran Village at Teldrassil's base. From there, coastal docks and flight paths connect the World Tree to other destinations.

subzone:temple-of-the-moon.text:
Temple of the Moon. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind guides her people from the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. The sanctuary is the seat of government on Teldrassil and home to the Sisterhood of Elune, whose priestesses tend a sacred moonwell. Built soon after the Third War, the Temple of the Moon rose as the night elves made their home on Teldrassil. It is among the largest stone works made by modern kaldorei hands. Its marble came from quarries on the Kalimdor mainland and crossed the sea by magical means.

At the temple's heart, a broad moonwell rests beneath the statue of Haidene. Pilgrims come to worship and reflect beside its consecrated waters. The temple also holds Darnassus's highest seat of government, where High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind guides her people through a new age. The priestesses of the Sisterhood of Elune serve their goddess from the temple terraces, in worship and in the field. Emissaries and dispatched sisters travel across northern Kalimdor to investigate threats or aid local sentinels. Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde, for example, makes inquiries along the Darkshore coastline.

Novices and veteran priestesses gather beneath the starry vaulted ceiling to learn divine spellwork, tend the wounded, and guard the sanctum from outside corruption.

subzone:the-loch.text: The Loch. The Loch's waters fill the heart of Loch Modan, held back by the Stonewrought Dam. The lake is Khaz Modan's largest body of water and sustains the dwarven settlements around it. At the center of Loch Modan, The Loch spreads among the largest inland lakes in the known world. Only Lordamere Lake and Darrowmere Lake to the north rival its size. Local fishermen draw from its waters, while Thelsamar and nearby hunting lodges enjoy a peaceful setting along its shores. Beneath the calm surface, aggressive threshadons and freshwater beasts make swimming across perilous. To the north, the Stonewrought Dam keeps The Loch in its tranquil state. The massive dwarven structure crosses a cleft in the mountains and prevents the lake from flooding into the Wetlands below. Its upkeep preserves the valley's ecosystem and helps keep Khaz Modan secure.

subzone:thelsamar.text: Thelsamar. In Thelsamar, travelers find shelter on the road between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands. The town keeps watch over the western bluffs above Loch Modan's great lake as troggs and ogres press nearby. Thelsamar gathers dwarven life beneath stout roofs of stone and timber. At the Stoutlager Inn, travelers can rest, and nearby they find a gryphon roost, crafting stations, and supply merchants. The town lies along the road from the South Gate Pass into Dun Morogh to the Algaz Pass toward the Wetlands. Travelers crossing the region pass through its doors. Trouble presses in on Thelsamar from several sides. Troggs pour from Stonesplinter Valley to the south, while bears and other predators haunt Grizzlepaw Ridge. Ironforge's regular forces are stretched thin across the realm. So the local magistrate and Mountaineers rely on travelers and mercenaries to patrol the trade roads and drive back hostile forces.

subzone:thistlefur-hold.text: Thistlefur Hold. At Thistlefur Hold, corruption has turned the furbolgs against every outsider who draws near. Their cavern den lies at the northern end of Thistlefur Village in west-central Ashenvale. At the northern end of Thistlefur Village, Thistlefur Hold lies at the heart of the Thistlefur tribe's territory. Corruption has driven the furbolgs mad, and they attack travelers and neighbors who draw near. In the winding caverns, the tribe hoards scavenged relics, including troll charms sought by the Darkspear. Deep within, wooden cages hold captives, among them Ruul Snowhoof, a tauren brave.

subzone:thistlefur-village.text: Thistlefur Village. In Ashenvale, Thistlefur furbolgs attack outsiders who approach their village north of Astranaar. Corruption has taken hold of the tribe, making the village dangerous to travelers. Among Ashenvale’s woodland communities, Thistlefur Village lies north of Astranaar. Corruption has maddened the Thistlefur furbolgs. They guard the paths through their settlement and attack travelers who draw near. Dal Bloodclaw and Rorgish Jowl lead the clan as fierce chieftains. Their aggression threatens nearby settlements and those traveling the roads.

subzone:thistlefuzz-arcanery.text: Thistlefuzz Arcanery. East of the Great Forge, Thistlefuzz Arcanery draws enchanters and scholars to a prominent gnome-run workshop and academy. Its chambers hum with arcane energy beside the fires of dwarven industry, offering a haven to those who weave magic into metal and parchment. East of the Great Forge, Thistlefuzz Arcanery offers a quieter craft beside the clanging anvils of dwarven smiths. Across its two levels, scholars, practitioners, and apprentices gather to study enchanting and the arcane arts. Dwarves reshape steel with muscle and fire, while the gnomes bind raw arcane energy into weapons, armor, and curious tools. For spellcasters making their way through the mountain stronghold, the Arcanery remains an essential sanctuary.

subzone:three-corners.text: Three Corners. At Three Corners, guards watch the western edge of the Redridge Mountains. Roads run from there to Goldshire, Lakeshire, and Darkshire, while gnolls threaten travelers and supply wagons. Three roads meet here, linking the southern settlements of Stormwind. Goldshire lies west in Elwynn Forest, Lakeshire northeast in Redridge, and Darkshire south in Duskwood. Stormwind built Tower Watch at the junction, where guards and scouts work to keep the roads clear. Gnolls from Redridge threaten travelers and supply wagons moving between the regions.

subzone:thunder-falls.text:
Thunder Falls. Bandits now hold a cottage beside the stream at Thunder Falls, high in northwestern Elwynn Forest. Above Mirror Lake, a mountain stream runs between the steep cliffs of Thunder Falls. From an unreachable cascade in the north, it spills down in falls on both sides. One pours into Mirror Lake, while the stream runs west toward Westfall’s rugged border.

A cottage, a dock, and an outdoor forge stand beside the water. Bandits now claim the clearing.

subzone:thunderbrew-distillery.text: Thunderbrew Distillery. In Kharanos, Thunderbrew Distillery offers travelers ale and shelter. Its brewhouse and tavern draw mountain travelers, while mentors and tradesfolk share their skills within. The Thunderbrew Distillery anchors Kharanos in southern Dun Morogh. Arkilus Thunderbrew founded its brewhouse, and his kin have kept it in the family. Its strong ales are known across Khaz Modan for warming those who face the mountain cold. Innkeeper Belm manages the inn, where weary mountaineers find a fire, hearty food, and beds beyond the blizzards outside. Kharanos is the first major settlement travelers reach after leaving Coldridge Valley. Beneath the distillery’s timber rafters, instructors teach martial arts, holy rites, arcane studies, and roguecraft. Teachers also offer cooking and first aid. The hall pours its well-known stouts and gives travelers a place to prepare for the road ahead.

subzone:tinker-town.text:
Tinker Town. Tinker Town is where gnomes make their home in exile beneath Ironforge. Since Gnomeregan fell, it has been the seat of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque’s government and the Ironforge end of the Deeprun Tram. Tinker Town shelters the gnomes who fled Gnomeregan. Troggs overran their high-tech city, so Ironforge’s dwarves opened their gates. They gave the refugees a cavern once used by dwarves, where the Deeprun Tram entrance already stood. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his council lead the gnomes from here.

Around a massive spherical contraption, the gnomes have rebuilt a semblance of their civilization. Gears whir, alchemy is tested, and gadgets take shape in the cramped district. Though guests in a stone city, the gnomes remain determined to reclaim their subterranean homeland. Tinker Town holds the Ironforge entrance to the Deeprun Tram. The engineering wonder carries travelers swiftly between the dwarven capital and Stormwind, joining the two cities.

subzone:tinkers-court.text: Tinkers' Court. In Gnomeregan's heart, Tinkers' Court once brought the city's leaders together. Now Mekgineer Thermaplugg holds the chamber. Before disaster drove the gnomes from Gnomeregan, their leaders gathered in Tinkers' Court. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque met there with advisors and master inventors, among them Tinkmaster Overspark. They debated new technology, governed civic matters, and guided gnomish society. Beyond the Engineering Labs and the Launch Bay, the chamber stood at the heart of gnomish government and invention.

subzone:tower-of-althalaxx.text: Tower of Althalaxx. Dark sorcery stirs at the Tower of Althalaxx on northern Darkshore's coast. Athrikus Narassin once withdrew there, and now demonic cultists and warlocks shelter within its ancient Highborne walls. Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne servants in Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran ten thousand years ago. She placed the powerful sorcerer Athrikus Narassin in authority over them. As Athrikus turned from civic governance, he withdrew to the nearby Tower of Althalaxx. The Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, yet the tower endured on Darkshore's desolate coast, a quiet ruin of forgotten elven magic.

subzone:tower-of-azora.text: Tower of Azora. At the Tower of Azora, Archmage Theocritus leads a scholarly outpost in eastern Elwynn Forest. The slender spire rises north of the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, where its human master keeps watch over a silent magical feud with a hostile tower in the Redridge Mountains. The Tower of Azora stands beside the eastern road to the Redridge Mountains. Gnome spellcasters staff most of the spire, where Archmage Theocritus guides their studies of strange curiosities and teaches wandering spellweavers. A wild magical aura surrounds the tower and sometimes warps nearby wildlife. Inside, gnome servants contend with enchanted household items and mutated insects that creep past the doorway.

subzone:tower-of-ilgalar.text: Tower of Ilgalar. In eastern Redridge, Morganth commands the Shadowhide gnolls from the Tower of Ilgalar. Banished from Stormwind, the sorcerer practices dark magic far from the city. Morganth holds the Tower of Ilgalar above eastern Redridge. Stormwind cast the sorcerer out of its Mage Quarter for forbidden magic. He withdrew to these heights to pursue the dark arts beyond imperial interference. The local Shadowhide gnolls guard the spire's base at his command. Inside, conjured demonic hounds stalk the halls, while shadowy power threatens Lakeshire below. The Tower of Ilgalar is often compared with the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest. No one knows who built Ilgalar, and the two towers face one another in quiet magical opposition. From Elwynn, the archmage Theocritus watches Ilgalar through enchanted devices such as the Eye of Azora. He studies Morganth's experiments and seeks to stop the sorcerer's corruption from spreading through the kingdom.

subzone:trade-district.text:
Trade District. Trade District draws merchants and travelers through Stormwind’s busy heart. Its bank, Auction House, guild registry, and shops serve citizens and adventurers alike. You pass beneath the stone arches from the Valley of Heroes into Trade District. The open plaza is Stormwind’s main marketplace and a crossroads for goods and travel. The Auction House stands at its center, with the Stormwind Counting House, the city’s main bank, and The Gilded Rose nearby.

From here, roads lead to Old Town, Cathedral Square, and the Mage Quarter. Coin, raw goods, and adventurers’ supplies pass through the district on their way across the realm. Shops line the paved avenues and canals with goods for daily needs and travel. Weller’s Arsenal and Lionheart Armory sell blades and mail, while The Empty Quiver offers bows. Stalls carry fresh flowers and aged vintages from the Gallina Winery.

Just inside the gates, the Stormwind Visitor’s Center handles newly registered guild charters and tabard designs. On the eastern side, an elevated ramp leads to the Gryphon Roost, linking Stormwind’s markets with Alliance territories.

subzone:tradesmen-s-terrace.text: Tradesmen's Terrace. Merchants and craftspeople gather in Tradesmen's Terrace along Darnassus's southern edge. Its auction house and shops connect travelers with goods from Teldrassil and beyond. Shops and merchants fill Darnassus's southern stretch in Tradesmen's Terrace. Kaldorei and travelers from across the Alliance find provisions, crafting supplies, and the city's central auction house here. Paths lead north to the Warrior's Terrace and west toward the Temple Gardens and the Temple of the Moon. Travelers bound for the wilds gather what they need here. Kaldorei shops favor quiet stone, timber, and woven goods shaped to live in harmony with nature. No roaring furnaces or smog rise from these workshops as they do in dwarven and human ones. Adventurers seeking trade contracts, repairs, or materials gathered from Teldrassil's boughs find northern Kalimdor's principal center of business here.

subzone:train-depot.text: Train Depot. Beneath Gnomeregan's entrance in Dun Morogh, the Train Depot lies overrun by leper gnomes and troggs. Once, its rails carried gnomes through the city. Now the depot is in ruin. Beneath the grand elevator from Dun Morogh, the Train Depot's platforms and tracks lie in ruin. Once, rail lines carried gnomes through Gnomeregan. Radiation swept through the city and changed the workers who remained into crazed leper gnomes. Troggs from below have overrun the rails. You must cross the depot to reach deeper parts of the city, including Clockwerk Run, the Loading Room, and the inner engineering facilities.

subzone:tranquil-gardens-cemetery.text: Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Southeast of Darkshire, Tranquil Gardens Cemetery is overrun by shambling skeletons and ghouls. The dead make it a danger to the nearby town. Once the people of Grand Hamlet laid their dead in Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Then dark curses settled over Duskwood, and the buried began clawing out of their plots. Skeletal warriors and mages haunt the gravestones, along with wandering undead. They are weaker than the horrors deeper in the woods, but their nearness to Darkshire makes them a constant threat to the townsfolk. Tranquil Gardens Cemetery lies near Darkshire's edge, where the Night Watch holds its line. The Watch sends fresh recruits and arriving adventurers to thin the rising dead before they reach the settlement. Yet more dangerous foes lurk among the tumbled headstones and the ruined chapel. The Insane Ghoul is one of them.

subzone:tundrid-hills.text: Tundrid Hills. In south-central Dun Morogh, the Tundrid Hills offer a perilous crossing west of Gol'Bolar Quarry. Snowbound ridges and dangerous wildlife make every step off the rocky passes a risk. From Coldridge Valley, the Tundrid Hills give you a rough way into eastern Dun Morogh, away from the main roads through Kharanos. Jagged slopes hold the snow, and the crossing is dangerous. Ferocious predators prowl the hills, so keep a weapon ready if you leave the beaten path.

subzone:twilight-grove.text:
Twilight Grove. At Duskwood's center, Twilight Grove shelters lush Kalimdor flora beneath its great tree. A moonwell and ancient night elf architecture surround a massive emerald gateway to the Emerald Dream. Behind steep crater ridges in Duskwood's heart, Twilight Grove seems utterly alien to the Eastern Kingdoms. Night elf gazebos and green meadows surround a serene moonwell. An unnamed great tree towers over the gloomy canopy.

The tree draws vigor from the Emerald Dream into the waking world. So the crater thrives beneath Duskwood's eternal gloom. At the great tree's base stands a massive stone portal, one of four known gateways linking the physical realm directly to the Emerald Dream. Ysera's green dragonflight traditionally watches over this gateway. Dark whispers say malevolent forces have begun twisting the tranquil realm beyond.

The gateway remains largely silent. Yet its emerald swirl warns that cosmic corruption may spill into Duskwood from paths deeper than the Scourge or the local worgen.

subzone:twilight-shore-darkshore.text: Twilight Shore (Darkshore). Murloc tribes and hungry sea creatures crowd Twilight Shore in southern Darkshore. Its rugged coast runs from the Long Wash to Ashenvale, where misty beaches meet cliffs, islets, and dangerous surf. Twilight Shore runs south from the Long Wash, past the ruins of Ameth'Aran, toward Ashenvale. Gray beaches give way to sharp cliffs and rocky islands. Threshadons and sea crawlers prowl the waters, while aggressive murloc camps line the shore.

subzone:twilight-vale.text:
Twilight Vale. In Twilight Vale, beasts and furbolgs prowl the dark woods between Darkshore and Ashenvale. The southern forest marks a perilous passage from Darkshore’s tainted coast to Ashenvale’s sacred canopies. Twilight Vale runs south from Ameth'Aran to the Ashenvale border, where dusk hangs over Darkshore’s southern woods. Corruption has spread deep among the wildlife. Rabid bears roam beside feral nightsabers, and hostile furbolg tribes stalk the trees.

Sentinels and travelers urge you to stay on the main road. A few paces into the woods can bring a swift, deadly ambush.

subzone:valley-of-heroes.text:
Valley of Heroes. In the Valley of Heroes, stone commanders watch the southern road into Stormwind. Guards hold this fortified crossing over the moat, where the city honors the leaders of the Alliance Expedition to Draenor. You cross the moat beneath statues honoring the Alliance Expedition’s commanders. Stormwind raised the monuments along this causeway as the city was rebuilt after the Second War. The champions marched through the Dark Portal into Draenor to seal the rift forever. They gave their lives so Azeroth might survive.

As you head north toward the Trade District, you pass Archmage Khadgar, Kurdran Wildhammer, Ranger-Captain Alleria Windrunner, Force Commander Danath Trollbane, and High General Turalyon. General Marcus Jonathan watches Stormwind's gates from horseback. He oversees the guards and the traffic passing in and out. The valley is the city's main defense against an overland invasion.

Major Mattingly, Field Marshal Stonebridge, and rows of seasoned guards keep watch beside him. Together, they guard the capital from threats beyond its walls.

subzone:valley-of-kings.text: Valley of Kings. At Valley of Kings, stone rulers guard the southern road into the Searing Gorge. In southwestern Loch Modan, the canyon lies south of the passage to Dun Morogh. Blackrock forces and troggs threaten travelers beneath the dwarven monuments. Two immense statues watch over the southern pass: King Madoran Bronzebeard and High Thane Khardros Wildhammer. After the kings died, their sons commissioned the carvings together. The statues honor the allied victory in the War of the Three Hammers, and they face the Dark Iron clan. Beyond them, the southern lands still bear the ruin left by Ragnaros's summoning. The valley links South Gate Pass with Stonesplinter Valley, and an iron gate opens into the Searing Gorge. Hostile Blackrock orcs, Dark Iron dwarves, and volcanic dangers make the passage perilous. So Ironforge mountaineers keep the gate locked and guarded, with Mountaineer Pebblebitty watching the threshold. Only the hardiest travelers may pass, after showing they have the strength to survive beyond it.

subzone:vault-of-ironforge.text: Vault of Ironforge. In Ironforge's Commons, citizens and Alliance travelers entrust their wealth to the Vault. Dinita and the Stonemantle family oversee its work. Travelers, soldiers, and merchants bring coin, relics, and provisions to the Vault for safekeeping. City guards and tellers watch the deposits, keeping the wealth of citizens and Alliance visitors secure within the mountain.

subzone:vul-gol-ogre-mound.text: Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. In southern Duskwood, Vul'Gol Ogre Mound shelters the Splinter Fist ogres and their chieftain, Zzarc'Vul. Ruined farmhouses and a cavern beneath the basin hold the clan's carcasses and scavenged plunder. Southwest of the fork toward Stranglethorn Vale, the basin belongs to the Splinter Fist clan. Human families once farmed here, but they fled or perished. Hollow cabins remain, and the ogres use them for shelter. In the cavern beneath the rise, slaughtered black bears lie in piles. Zzarc'Vul rules the encampment, keeping odd trinkets beside ordinary goods the clan has scavenged. Darkshire's Night Watch is stretched thin, guarding the town from rabid worgen and restless dead. Commander Althea Ebonlocke and her militia rely on outside mercenaries to thin the Splinter Fist ranks before the ogres push north. The clan has also raided the recluse Abercrombie and stolen a crate of his alchemical tools. Inquisitive mages seek arcane lenses that Zzarc'Vul is rumored to possess.

subzone:war-room.text:
War Room. Commanders gather inside Stormwind Keep to plan the Alliance’s defense. The War Room holds weapons, records, and charts for that work. Beyond Stormwind Keep’s grand chambers, commanders plan campaigns and arrange military supplies. Swords, blunderbusses, and heavy artillery cannons line the stone walls. Nearby tables hold military treatises and chronicles of past wars.

At the center, a large map shows Alliance deployments across Azeroth. The royal court handles affairs of state just steps away.

subzone:warrior-s-terrace.text:
Warrior's Terrace. Sentinels guard the eastern gate at Warrior's Terrace, where drills and duels fill the plazas. The district is Darnassus's military heart, with battlemasters and warrior trainers overlooking the road into greater Teldrassil. Sentinels guard Darnassus from the Warrior's Terrace, also called the Hall of Justice. Mounted on nightsabers, they watch the high arched gates for travelers from Teldrassil's wilds. In the open plazas, aspiring combatants drill beside seasoned veterans on dueling grounds and target ranges.

Weapon smiths and armorers serve practical military needs. Battlemasters coordinate night elf forces across the wider world.

subzone:warsong-labor-camp.text: Warsong Labor Camp. Warsong loggers cut Ashenvale timber at Warsong Labor Camp to supply the growing Horde. They work in the southeast, far from help and under threat from the forest's defenders. East of Fallen Sky Lake and southwest of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, Warsong loggers cut Ashenvale's dense timber. Durotar's dry plains offer little wood for building cities such as Orgrimmar, so the Warsong clan has entered these contested woods. Far from other Horde settlements, loggers and orcish guards fell ancient trees while night elf scouts and Alliance warbands threaten the camp. Warsong Labor Camp lies far from the main road and fortified bases such as Splintertree Post. Alliance raiders strike its working peons and watchmen, knowing help may be slow to arrive. Night elves see each felled tree as a desecration. So the camp remains a point of conflict in the war.

subzone:warsong-lumber-camp.text:
Warsong Lumber Camp. Warsong Lumber Camp cuts Ashenvale timber for the Horde and keeps its conflict with the night elves alive. Kargathia Keep guards the operation. In eastern Ashenvale, Warsong Lumber Camp cuts through the dense canopy for the Horde. Orc peons and hired goblin engineers drive whirring shredders through towering trunks, making lumber for nearby Splintertree Post and the fledgling nation of Durotar.

Kargathia Keep anchors the camp's defenses against night elf counterattacks. War wolves wait in an active kennel. To the Warsong, every felled tree means survival and strength. To the native Sentinels, each saw blade is an act of sacrilege. Warsong clan warriors first entered these woods with Grom Hellscream during the Third War, seeking timber for the Horde. Their clearing enraged the demigod Cenarius and drew the ancient wrath of the night elves.

Now Thrall's Horde banners fly over the camp, but old hatreds still burn. Untamed timber, hostile elves, and demonic corruption around neighboring Felfire Hill surround it. Its defenders stay armed around the clock, axes in hand as they harvest, ready to abandon the lumber when the next ambush comes.

subzone:weathered-nook.text: Weathered Nook. High above Thousand Needles, Dorn Plainstalker and Prate Cloudseer make their home in a quiet cliffside shelter. From there, they look out across the stone spires, far from the canyon floor. North of Freewind Post, a narrow ramp climbs the sandstone cliff to a sheltered ledge and cave. From below, travelers can easily miss the Weathered Nook high above the canyon basin. Dorn Plainstalker and Prate Cloudseer live here, away from any large settlement or military post. The ledge shelters them from the prevailing winds and gives them a broad view across the needle plateaus.

subzone:webwinder-path.text: Webwinder Path. Webwinder Path carries travelers through the lower Stonetalon Mountains, from Malaka'jin toward Mirkfallon Lake. Spiders and native beasts roam its crags and woods. Thick webs hang among the trees and cling to jagged cliffs along Webwinder Path. Mountain spiders prowl the road, while thunder lizards and territorial rams roam nearby. Watch your step as the route winds through the lower Stonetalon Mountains.

subzone:wellspring-lake.text:
Wellspring Lake. In northern Teldrassil, Wellspring Lake’s waters flow north as corruption troubles the wildlife. Northeast of Darnassus, the lake once offered night elf fishermen a quiet retreat. Beneath Teldrassil’s canopy, Wellspring Lake lies between Darnassus and the Oracle Glade. Night elves once came to its clear waters to fish and sit in quiet thought. Springs deep within the World Tree feed the lake, whose waters flow north through the Wellspring River.

Now a blight troubles the surrounding wilds. Aggressive spiders, prowling nightsabers, and agitated timberlings roam the banks, making the shore dangerous for travelers.

subzone:wellspring-river.text:
Wellspring River. In Teldrassil, Wellspring River carries water north from Wellspring Lake and over the World Tree's edge to the sea. Timberlings along its banks have grown dangerous. Wellspring River runs north from Wellspring Lake through Teldrassil's forest. At the edge of the great tree, its waters plunge to the sea below.

The riverbanks have grown unsafe. Timberlings there have gone crazed, attacking travelers and druids who come near the water.

subzone:westbrook-garrison.text:
Westbrook Garrison. At Westbrook Garrison, Deputy Rainer's few guards watch Elwynn's western road. Gnolls and bandits threaten the border, and the outpost lacks the men and supplies to hold it alone. Westbrook Garrison watches the road where Elwynn Forest thins toward Westfall. Deputy Rainer and a handful of guards patrol the western roads, too few to cover them. Much of the Stormwind Army serves abroad, and indecision in the capital leaves the outpost without needed support.

Thieves grow bolder, and Riverpaw gnolls have overrun the southern woods. Marshal Dughan in Goldshire has sent no formal reinforcements, so the guards depend on travelers to help secure the highway. Riverpaw gnolls gather south of Forest's Edge, raiding supply lines and homesteads. The packs follow Hogger, a fearsome chieftain whose forces outnumber the garrison and overwhelm its guards with brute strength.

A high bounty is posted across the outpost. It seeks fighters willing to enter the hills and bring down Hogger before the gnolls press farther east.

subzone:westfall-lighthouse.text: Westfall Lighthouse. Westfall Lighthouse stands dark on the rocky isle off Westfall's southwestern shore, and its keepers are gone. Old Murk-Eye led the attack that killed them. Captain Grayson's spirit remains by the tower. Westfall Lighthouse once guided ships past Westfall's dangerous southwestern bluffs and along the coast near Stormwind. As law and order failed across the region, royal patrols dwindled and coastal dangers grew unchecked. Murloc tribes drove the keepers inland. The family returned to relight the beacon, but Old Murk-Eye rallied his kin to attack again. The murlocs killed the keepers and put out the light.

subzone:whelgar-s-excavation-site.text: Whelgar's Excavation Site. On a ridge above Whelgar's Excavation Site, dwarven prospectors are cut off from their findings. Mottled raptors overran the quarry where they sought ancient fossils and clues to the distant past. Between Menethil Harbor and Dun Modr, dwarven prospectors dug for ancient fossils and earthen mysteries. Their search stirred the native mottled raptors. Overwhelmed and under-equipped, the archaeologists fled to a ridge overlooking the site. Their tents, tools and unearthed relics remain among the prowling predators.

subzone:whitereach-post.text: Whitereach Post. Horde travelers find rest at Whitereach Post beside the canyon path in Thousand Needles. Near Camp E'thok, the small camp overlooks the harsh road between Feralas and the salt flats beneath the sandstone pillars. Whitereach Post watches over the canyon road through Thousand Needles. Near Camp E'thok, this modest Horde foothold is one of several posts in the rugged wastes. Scouts monitor travel along the canyon floor between the mesas. Couriers and travelers crossing the contested wastes can stop here, though the post has fewer defenses than the great lift or the major tribal settlements.

subzone:wildbend-river.text: Wildbend River. Near the Grove of the Ancients, Wildbend River carries demonic poison toward the sea. Its waters cross southern Darkshore from the corrupted heights of Felwood and threaten the wilderness. Wildbend River carries corruption through southern Darkshore. It runs west past the Grove of the Ancients and empties into the sea. The stream begins as Felwood's Bloodvenom River, then tumbles through rocky ridges with foul runoff. Night elves watch its banks for twisted wildlife and spreading demonic blight.

subzone:windshear-crag.text: Windshear Crag. In central Stonetalon, Windshear Crag lies stripped by the Venture Company's logging. Machinery and muddy runoff have replaced the old forest. Kobolds dig for ore nearby, and a mountain path leads beneath the ridges to Ashenvale. The Venture Company cut down Windshear Crag's old forest for profit. Stumps and machinery now fill the basin. From a platform above Cragpool Lake, Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle oversees the logging. The leper gnome's engineering gave the company the Super Reaper 6000, a machine that fells great trees in moments. As the operation strips the mountain bare, rival engineers and local inhabitants grow angry. Logging is not the only danger or crossing at Windshear Crag. In the southeast, kobolds dig through Windshear Mine for Smoky Iron Ingots. They attack those who come near their haul. From the crag's northeast reaches, the Talondeep Path runs beneath the ridges into Ashenvale. Near its entrance, the tauren elder Braug Dimspirit tests the historical wisdom and resolve of Horde travelers crossing the contested peaks.

subzone:xavian.text:
Xavian. At Xavian in northeastern Ashenvale, satyrs hold an ancient night elf temple. They make it their chief seat in the forest and use its ruins for dark rites that spread demonic corruption through the woodland. In Ashenvale's northeastern hills, Xavian lies west of Forest Song and north of Satyrnaar. Satyrs hold its ruined temple, once sacred to the night elves, and make it their chief stronghold in the forest. Their leaders, including Prince Raze and Geltharis, direct their followers from its desecrated arches and terraces.

Across the grounds, satyrs perform rites against the woodland and use stolen Warsong oil to blight it. The place bears the name of Xavius, a highborne councilor who became the first satyr during the War of the Ancients after failing Sargeras.

subzone:yorgen-farmstead.text: Yorgen Farmstead. Defias outlaws hold Yorgen Farmstead in southern Duskwood. Sven Yorgen fled north to a camp along the Darkened Bank. Yorgen Farmstead lies in southern Duskwood, where Sven Yorgen once worked the land. Danger drove him north to a makeshift camp along the Darkened Bank. Outlaws took the farm after he left, seeking ground beyond Stormwind's reach. The Defias Brotherhood uses Yorgen Farmstead as a staging ground. Masked highwaymen and cutthroats hide among its fences and outbuildings, screened by dense trees. Defias assassins patrol the grounds and ambush travelers who trespass.

subzone:zoram-gar-outpost.text: Zoram'gar Outpost. Horde forces hold the western shore of Ashenvale at Zoram'gar Outpost. From this fortified beachhead, they watch the Zoram Strand and the dangers beyond it. Zoram'gar Outpost holds Ashenvale's northwestern edge, where forest meets sea. Night elf territory lies inland, and hazards wait offshore. Scouts, hunters, and shaman keep watch from the isolated camp. Naga prowl the shallows, while cultists and primal horrors stir in Blackfathom Deeps, the cavern system down the shore. Zoram'gar Outpost links by flight to other Horde holdings: Splintertree Post, the Crossroads, and Thunder Bluff. Though small, the camp anchors Horde supply lines along Ashenvale's western coast.

subzone:zoram-strand.text: Zoram Strand. At Ashenvale's northwestern edge, Zoram Strand faces the Veiled Sea. The shore's ancient night elven ruins now lie beneath Wrathtail naga, shipwrecks, and beached leviathans. Blackfathom Deeps begins in the submerged temple complex nearby. Ten thousand years ago, the night elven city of Zoram stood on this coast. Then the Great Sundering tore Kalimdor apart and sank the settlement beneath the sea. Now the tide carries ancient relics, shattered vessels, and the carcasses of massive sea beasts onto the shore. Wrathtail naga overrun the beaches and tidal pools, guarding the flooded ruins and ancient artifacts from anyone who comes near. Travelers from the mainland and along the coast still come to Zoram Strand despite the naga. South of the shore, the Horde holds Zoram'gar Outpost, where its warriors fight to secure the coast. Nearby, Blackfathom Deeps lies deep within the caverns. The ancient temple of Elune has fallen into dark hands, drawing scouts, scholars, and treasure seekers who brave the surf.
